*All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. In this connection, at the time of your application, please answer the following question: Are you a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of Canada? (Yes/No)*

The terms and conditions of this appointment, including salary, are governed by the collective agreement between the Faculty Association of the University of Calgary and the Governors of the University of Calgary. Detailed information is available [here](https://www.ucalgary.ca/hr/work-compensation/collective-agreements-and-handbooks/tucfa-collective-agreement).

For a listing of all academic opportunities at the University of Calgary, view our [Academic Careers website](http://careers.ucalgary.ca/pages/academic-careers). For more information about the Faculty of Arts, click [*here*](https://arts.ucalgary.ca/).

About the University of Calgary

UCalgary is Canada's entrepreneurial university, located in Canada's most enterprising city. It is a top research university and one of the highest-ranked universities of its age. Founded in 1966, its 36,000 students experience an innovative learning environment, made rich by research, hands-on experiences and entrepreneurial thinking. It is [Canada's leader in the creation of start-ups](https://ucalgary.ca/news/ucalgary-top-startup-creator-amongst-research-institutions-canada). [Start something](https://www.ucalgary.ca/startsomething) today at the University of Calgary. For more information, visit [ucalgary.ca](https://www.ucalgary.ca/).

The university's commitment to the Indigenous Strategy is evident through the oversight of 18 Elders serving on the Circle of Advisors and the many unit-based circles working towards implementation of the strategy including the Faculty Advisory Circle and teams such as the Office of Indigenous Engagement, the Writing Symbols Lodge, and the Indigenous Research Support Team. Many Indigenous-based events and processes are impacting curriculum, programming and polices at the University of Calgary.

About Calgary, Alberta

Calgary is one of the world's cleanest cities and has been named one of the world's most livable cities for years. Calgary is a city of leaders - in business, community, philanthropy and volunteerism. Calgarians benefit from a growing number of world-class dining and cultural events and enjoy more days of sunshine per year than any other major Canadian city. Calgary is less than an hour's drive from the majestic Rocky Mountains and boasts the most extensive urban pathway and bikeway network in North America.

With a growing urban Indigenous population of approximately 50,000 people, there are several Indigenous organizations and many events and ceremonies taking place in the city throughout the year.

**POSITION DESCRIPTION**

The Department of Management at the University of Toronto Scarborough (UTSC) invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Environmental Economics. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.

This position is part of the Canada Excellence Research Chair Network for Equity in Sustainability Transitions (CERC-NEST). The [CERC NEST](https://cercnest.ca/) uses a transdisciplinary, comparative and action-centred approach with communities and city actors in Toronto and internationally to examine how to enhance participation in decision-making, address inequities in regulations and investments, and ensure fair distribution of benefits, livability and a good life for all. The successful candidate will contribute economic perspectives and methods to this agenda, with particular attention to the distributional, procedural, and recognition of the dimensions of climate and sustainability policies and interventions.

This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members ([Statement on Equity, Diversity and Excellence](https://governingcouncil.utoronto.ca/secretariat/policies/equity-diversity-and-excellence-statement)). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.

In addition, the University of Toronto Scarborough is implementing its Strategic Plan: [Inspiring Inclusive Excellence](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/principal/sites/utsc.utoronto.ca.principal/files/docs/UTSC%20Strategic%20Plan%202020.pdf). Consistent with the values and objectives in that plan, we especially welcome candidates who self-identify as Indigenous or those who have lived experience in Black or other racialized (persons of colour) communities. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to be connected with colleagues from under-represented groups, including those hired through targeted efforts in recent years across departments spanning the Sciences, Social Sciences, and Humanities.

**REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS**

Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Economics, by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in environmental economics. Candidates should have an academic concentration and research program that are directly related to environmental economics. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing [departmental strengths](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/faculty), dovetail with [CERC NEST](https://cercnest.ca/) research vision and methodologies, and contribute to [campus](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/home/) strengths and priorities. Relevant areas may include, but are not limited to, environmental and energy policy, climate economics, environmental regulation, sustainable transportation, urban environmental economics, and the distributional impacts of sustainability interventions. Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals, forthcoming publications, or working papers that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees of high standing in the candidate’s field.

Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters.

Equity and diversity are essential to academic excellence. We seek candidates who value diversity and whose research, teaching and service bear out our commitment to equity. Candidates must also show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and to the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment, as demonstrated through the application materials. Candidates are asked to submit a 1- to 2-page statement of contributions to equity and diversity, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): research or teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities, the development of inclusive pedagogies, or the mentoring of students from underrepresented groups.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program. Grounded in the CERC-NEST goal of co-producing knowledge to foster equity in sustainability transitions, the successful candidate will be expected to integrate perspectives from economics into research and teaching on equity and justice in energy and sustainability transitions, including the evaluation of the distributional, procedural, and recognition dimensions of sustainability interventions. The successful candidate will also be expected to collaborate across disciplines and, where appropriate, engage with communities, city actors, and other partners involved in CERC-NEST research.

In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.

Responsibilities also include advancing the area's research agenda, teaching undergraduate students at the University of Toronto Scarborough, and active involvement in PhD student education and training.

**HIRING SALARY RANGE**

The salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The salary range for this position exceeds $200,000 CAD per annum.

**ABOUT US**

The successful candidate will conduct and publish independent scholarly research in nationally and internationally recognized outlets through a research agenda that contributes to the analysis of market-based solutions to societal challenges, as described under Qualifications.

The successful candidate will make significant contributions to the department’s teaching mission through course development and delivery to undergraduate and graduate students in one or more fields of economics specialization. The general teaching load is 2 courses per year, 1 in one semester and 1 in the other. The successful candidate will also supervise and mentor graduate students, including thesis and dissertation research as well as serve on departmental committees; and participate in the academic and administrative affairs of the Department and in university, professional, national, and international service as appropriate to rank.

The Department of Economics at UW-Madison is highly rated and is a leader in its field, generally ranked in the top 15 economics departments in the nation. Our department is multidisciplinary and has a highly collaborative environment. The Department values open inquiry, rigorous debate, and scholarly engagement with competing explanations and institutional approaches.

**Key job responsibilities:**

Conduct and publish independent scholarly research in nationally and internationally recognized outlets through a research agenda that contributes to the analysis of market-based solutions to societal challenges

Participate in the academic and administrative affairs of the Department and in university, professional, national, and international service as appropriate to rank.

Contributions to course development and delivery for undergraduates and graduates.

Supervise and mentor graduate students, including thesis and dissertation research

**Required qualifications:**

The search is broad with respect to field and methodology, while focused on research that takes market institutions, competition, incentives, or alternative institutional arrangements as central objects of analysis in addressing societal challenges. Relevant topics include but are not limited to: competition and market power; property rights and contracting; entrepreneurship and innovation; the design, effects, and limits of regulation; institutional and mechanism design; decentralized information and price formation; and market-based approaches to policy problems.

Applicants should have research underway that demonstrates the potential to produce high-quality publications and make a lasting impact in their field of specialization and should demonstrate the potential for excellence in teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels. In addition, the successful candidate will demonstrate fostering or the ability to foster a teaching, learning, mentoring, departmental, and research environment where all can thrive.

a letter of application

a combined research, teaching, and mentoring statement

a job market paper

The [Initiative for Financial Decision-Making (IFDM)](https://ifdm.stanford.edu/) at the Stanford Graduate School of Business invites applications for a Postdoctoral Fellow to work with Professor Annamaria Lusardi, the Initiative’s faculty director. This in-person position begins in summer 2027, no later than September 1, 2027. The initial appointment is for one year and may be renewed for a second year subject to performance at or above expectations. A two-year term is strongly preferred.

The fellowship focuses on empirical research in financial literacy and household financial decision-making. Although IFDM is a relatively new initiative, its work draws on more than a decade of research in this field by the Global Financial Literacy Excellence Center (GFLEC), founded by Professor Lusardi. GFLEC has developed tools to measure financial literacy and conducted research that informs financial education programs in the United States and internationally. Over the past three years, IFDM has built on that foundation with research of its own on household financial decisions and financial education, expanding the scope of this shared research agenda.

The fellow will contribute to projects in three related areas:  
• Household financial decisions: Study how financial literacy shapes saving, investing, and borrowing choices, and financial well-being outcomes, including how young adults begin investing and build wealth early in life. Projects may also examine how emerging financial products affect the allocation of savings across investments.  
• Financial education programs: Evaluate the effects of financial education programs and initiatives on financial knowledge, behavior, and outcomes, including through field experiments.  
• Financial education in schools and higher education: Study the availability of financial education courses and related offerings, and the factors shaping their supply and demand.

The fellow will develop academic research within this agenda and work with Professor Lusardi, IFDM’s research director and associate director, coauthors, PhD students, and other postdoctoral fellows. The role combines collaborative and independent research. The fellow will present research progress regularly to Initiative stakeholders and participate in meetings, research lunches, and colloquia. Located in downtown Toronto, the largest and most culturally diverse city in Canada and on the territory of the *Anishinaabeg, Haudenosaunee, Mississaugas of the Credit and the Wendat Peoples,* the Department of Economics in the [Faculty of Arts](http://www.torontomu.ca/arts) at [Toronto Metropolitan University](http://torontomu.ca/) [[www.torontomu.ca](http://www.torontomu.ca/)] invites applications for a tenure track position at the rank of Assistant Professor effective July 1, 2027 subject to final budgetary approval.

The successful candidate will engage in a combination of teaching, research, and service duties while maintaining an inclusive, equitable, and collegial work environment across all activities. Teaching duties will entail teaching at undergraduate and graduate levels, supervision of students and curriculum development. The successful candidate will pursue a strong, innovative research program that is externally funded and that produces cutting-edge, high quality results.

* a commitment to our values of equity, diversity, and inclusion as it pertains to service, teaching, and scholarly, research or creative activities, including a demonstrated ability to make learning accessible and inclusive for a diverse student population; and
* an ability and willingness to contribute to the life of the Department of Economics and the University through collegial service.

This position falls under the jurisdiction of the Toronto Metropolitan Faculty Association (TFA) [[www.tfanet.ca](http://www.tfanet.ca/)]. Visit us at [www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs](http://www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs) to view the [TFA collective agreement](https://www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs/resources/documents/collective-agreements/tfa-collective-agreement/) and a summary of [TFA benefits](https://www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs/employment-at-tmu/life-and-work-at-tmu/why-tmu/). At the intersection of mind and action, TMU is on a transformative path to become Canada’s leading comprehensive innovation university. Our new academic plan, [*Transformative Futures*](https://www.torontomu.ca/content/dam/provost/academic-plan/tmu-academic-plan.pdf), offers an exciting roadmap towards our ongoing pursuit of academic excellence and to addressing the complex and evolving challenges of our time.

At the heart of TMU’s remarkable achievements and its ambitious aspirations are its students, faculty and staff. Committed to a people first culture, the university prides itself on offering exceptional [benefits and perks](https://www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs/employment-at-tmu/life-and-work-at-tmu/why-tmu/), [celebrating the achievements of its faculty and staff](https://www.torontomu.ca/recognition-awards/) and maintaining its unwavering commitment to [equity, diversity and inclusion](https://www.torontomu.ca/equity/about-ovpeci/), including its ongoing commitment to [Truth and Reconciliation](https://www.torontomu.ca/provost/strategic-plans/academic-plan/priorities/truth-reconciliation/), [confronting Anti-Black Racism](https://www.torontomu.ca/equity/programs-reports/confronting-anti-black-racism/) and [accessibility](https://www.torontomu.ca/accessibility/) for persons with disabilities. TMU’s growing reputation and global reach—reflected in its [performance across select national and international rankings](https://www.torontomu.ca/about/rankings/)—support its mission to address real-world challenges, attract top talent and strengthen impact across teaching, research and innovation. Among its many recognitions include being ranked number one on the [Forbes list](https://www.forbes.com/sites/rachelpeachman/2023/07/11/meet-canadas-best-employers-for-diversity-2023/?sh=4b23e3b918c3) of Canada’s Best Employers for Diversity. We invite you to [explore employment at TMU](https://www.torontomu.ca/faculty-affairs/employment-at-tmu/) as well as our community of diverse [faculty and staff networks](https://www.torontomu.ca/equity/community-networks-committees/).

Connect with us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/school/torontometropolitanuniversity/) for the latest news and opportunities at TMU.

**Department of Economics**
---------------------------

The Department of Economics offers undergraduate and graduate (Master’s and Doctoral) programs to students of diverse backgrounds. Our faculty prides itself on the excellence of its research activities and the quality of its teaching. We are interested in candidates who will contribute to the Department of Economics’ existing strengths and assist in advancing its priorities. Please visit our website to learn more: <https://www.torontomu.ca/economics/>

**How to Apply**

Applicants must submit their application online via Econ Job Market ([http://EconJobMarket.org](http://econjobmarket.org/)). Applications, consisting of the following, must be received **by November 13, 2026**:

* a letter of application;
* a curriculum vitae;

Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, applications from Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority, in accordance with Canadian immigration regulations.

At Toronto Metropolitan University, we believe that diversity of knowledge, worldviews and experiences that come from membership in different groups, is fundamental to innovation, teaching and scholarship and that our students are best served by faculty who reflect the diversity of TMU’s student body and the community in which TMU is situated. To ensure representation of the excellent talent in Canada, we are particularly interested in applications from members of historically disadvantaged and marginalized groups including: First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples, Indigenous peoples of North America\*, Black-identified persons, other racialized persons, persons with disabilities, and those who identify as women and/or 2SLGBTQ+.

\* Applicants who self-identify as First Nations, Métis, Inuit peoples, or Indigenous peoples of North America will be invited to complete an affirmation process at TMU. This process involves candidates providing relevant documentation to support the claim of Indigenous identity and participating in discussions with the University’s Indigenous Human Resources Lead in order to share relevant information about their lived experience.

Faculty Position in International Economics, Open Rank

Location: Qatar

Open Date: Sep 22, 2026

Description

Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) invites applications for one (1) open-rank core faculty position in International Economics.

We welcome applications from candidates in all fields of economics, with a preference for candidates conducting applied and empirically relevant research. This may include, but is not limited to, fields such as international economics, development economics, behavioral economics, labor economics, political economy, and applied microeconomics and macroeconomics. Applicants should demonstrate a strong research profile, evidenced by a substantial record of high-quality research accomplishments or, for more junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to develop such a record. Candidates should also have an ambitious and active research agenda and a strong record of teaching excellence.

Appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, depending on the candidate's experience and qualifications.

Qualifications

- A Ph.D. in Economics.

- A strong and active research agenda, with a demonstrated record of publication in leading economics journals or, for junior candidates, clear evidence of the potential to establish such a record.

- A strong commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring, demonstrated through previous teaching experience and, for senior candidates, a sustained record of teaching effectiveness and student mentorship.

Academic Environment and Faculty Support

GU-Q offers a rich academic setting supported by strong institutional resources to enable excellence in teaching and research. Faculty typically teach two courses (or 6 credit hours) per semester (a 2-2 load), supported by best-in-class instructional infrastructure. This includes the Global Classroom, which connects students in Doha with peers in Washington, D.C., for live, cross-campus engagement, and access to collaborative research centers such as the <https://cirs.georgetown.edu/>.

To advance faculty scholarship and professional development, GU-Q provides:

- Access to GU-Q faculty research funds.

- Eligibility for funding through the <https://qrdi.org.qa/en-us/>.

- Eligibility to apply for a summer research supplement equivalent to 2/9 of base salary.

- Generous conference travel funding and professional development resources.

Compensation and Benefits

GU-Q offers a highly competitive compensation package by U.S. academic standards, along with an exceptional <https://hr.qatar.georgetown.edu/employee-benefits/> that includes:

- Fully furnished, high-quality housing.

- Transportation allowance.

- Annual family home leave.

- Worldwide health insurance coverage.

- Private school tuition support for accompanying children.

- Additional relocation and onboarding assistance.

About Georgetown University in Qatar

GU-Q was established in 2005 alongside other elite international universities in <https://www.qf.org.qa/education/education-city>, in partnership with Qatar Foundation. GU-Q is an integral part of Georgetown University, delivering the renowned School of Foreign Service's <https://www.qatar.georgetown.edu/academics/programs/bachelor-science-foreign-service-bsfs-degree-program/> (BSFS) degree. Ranked <https://foreignpolicy.com/2024/07/30/international-relations-school-rankings-university-undergraduate-masters-phd-programs/> in international relations by Foreign Policy magazine, this liberal arts program offers majors in International Politics, International History, Culture and Politics, International Economics, and Science, Technology, and International Affairs. The degree is awarded by Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. GU-Q is a research-focused, student-oriented institution with a globally competitive research and publications record. GU-Q values interdisciplinarity, and its faculty and students benefit from the opportunities offered by the wider academic ecosystem of Education City. For more information on GU-Q, see <https://www.qatar.georgetown.edu/>.

Life in Qatar

Qatar offers a diverse, family-friendly living environment, with the cultural, educational, and recreational resources of a major global city. Public parks, beaches, sports facilities (including Education City's extensive sports venues), <https://qm.org.qa/en/>, cafes, and restaurants abound, and a state-of-the-art metro system connects all parts of Doha and nearby locations. Within Education City, the iconic <https://www.qnl.qa/en>, designed by Rem Koolhaas, provides free membership to faculty and students. Faculty at GU-Q also benefit from a close-knit Georgetown community, strong institutional support, and regular coordination between Doha and Washington, D.C. While the early months of 2026 brought instability to the region, Doha remains one of the safest cities in the world, and Qatar continues to rank highly in the <https://www.visionofhumanity.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Global-Peace-Index-2026-Report.pdf>. Doha is connected by direct flights to more than 160 destinations in 90 countries. This <https://youtu.be/HNoERrWln4k> offers a glimpse of what it is like to teach and live in Qatar.

Application Process

Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applicants should provide a cover letter detailing teaching and research interests, curriculum vitae, the names and contact details of three scholarly references, and, if available, evidence of teaching excellence (such as recent student course ratings, peer observation reports, etc.).

All application materials must be submitted via Georgetown's online application management system at <https://apply.interfolio.com/194081>.

Questions about the online application system should be directed to Ms. Carina Lawson at cl978@georgetown.edu. Queries about the position should be directed to Professor Ramon Cobo Reyes Cano at rc1557@georgetown.edu. Please reference "International Economics" in the subject line.

Application Instructions

For more information and to apply, visit <https://apptrkr.com/9885596>

GU is an <https://policymanual.hr.georgetown.edu/200-hiring-and-employment/201-equal-employment-opportunity-affirmative-action/>. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, citizenship, color, disability, family responsibilities, gender identity and expression, genetic information, marital status, matriculation, national origin, race, religion, personal appearance, political affiliation, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic <https://georgetown.box.com/s/jkc3kxwrf56e1n2km0jh1vj09fvanw70>.

Requesting Accommodations

If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need reasonable accommodations for any part of the application and hiring process, please visit the Office for Equal Opportunity Compliance website for <https://oeoc.georgetown.edu/ada/>, as well as <https://oeoc.georgetown.edu/ada/applicants/>. **Ad text:**

The Faculty of Management, Economics and Social Sciences at the University of Fribourg (Switzerland) invites applications for an

**Assistant Professorship in the Economics of Sustainability (tenure-track)**

at the Department of Economics. The expected start date is August 1 or September 1, 2027.

The successful candidate will teach courses in German and English at the Bachelor’s and Master’s levels. At the Bachelor level, the successful candidate is expected to offer a course in Public Economics in German. The research profile as well as offered Master courses should fall within the domain of sustainability, including, for example, climate, energy or environmental economics, but could also include societal elements of sustainability, such as poverty, inequality or well-being.

The successful candidate must hold a Ph.D. in Economics or a related field (or expect to complete the Ph.D. prior to commencing the position in Fribourg). Further, the candidate must demonstrate strong research potential in the economics of sustainability, the ability to publish in leading journals, and excellent teaching skills. The University of Fribourg is bilingual (French/German). Fluency in German is required and knowledge of French (oral level B1) is expected. If knowledge of French is lacking, it must be acquired within two years of taking up the position.

The position includes one 100% doctoral assistant. The University offers attractive working conditions and a competitive salary. Seeking to promote an equitable representation of women and men, the University strongly encourages applications from women. Having signed the CoARA declaration, the University of Fribourg emphasizes qualitative assessment of academic achievement.

Candidates should submit a complete application package (motivation letter, CV (including potential career breaks, list of publications and, if applicable, information about third-party funding and administrative experience), research and teaching statement, three recommendation letters, a job market paper, and teaching evaluations if available) **by November 5th, 2026.**

All applications are to be submitted through www.econjobmarket.org.

Inquiries can be sent to [sustain-econ@unifr.ch](mailto:sustain-econ@unifr.ch), or to Prof. Holger Herz via [holger.herz@unifr.ch](mailto:holger.herz@unifr.ch).

**Ad text:**

The Faculty of Economics and Social Sciences and the Heidelberg Center for American Studies at Heidelberg University invite applications for a
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Full professorship (W3) in “American Studies” (f/m/d)**

with an expected start date of April 1, 2028.

We are looking for excellent candidates from the social sciences (in particular, sociology, political science, economics/economic history, or media studies) with a strong focus on the United States.

**Your responsibilities:**

The core responsibilities of the professorship in research and teaching are at the Heidelberg Center for American Studies (HCA). The HCA is a central academic institution of Heidelberg University and brings together expertise on the US from various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences. Applicants should also demonstrate the ability and willingness to serve as director of the HCA.

**Your qualifications:**

The appointment requires a university degree, a qualified doctorate, pedagogical aptitude which is usually proven by teaching experience, and (in accordance with Article 47, paragraph 2 of the Higher Education Law of the state of Baden-Württemberg) a habilitation, a successfully evaluated junior professorship or equivalent qualifications.

We are looking for candidates who have an outstanding and internationally visible track record of working within the interdisciplinary context of American Studies and who are well connected in this field. Experience in collaborative research projects and in acquiring third-party funding is required.

**What we offer:**

The post in question is a leading professorship. Its holder will be expected to maintain and enhance the international research profile of the HCA. The financial/staff/equipment resources associated with the post are geared to its special significance for Heidelberg University.

If you have any questions about the job posting, please contact Prof. Dr. Ulrike Gerhard ([u.gerhard@uni-heidelberg.de](mailto:u.gerhard@uni-heidelberg.de)) and/or Prof. Dr. Jan Stievermann ([jstievermann@hca.uni-heidelberg.de](mailto:jstievermann@hca.uni-heidelberg.de)).

Please submit your application (CV, including a list of publications, a list of courses taught, a state of research interests and objectives, list of third-party funding, copies of certificates and transcripts) as one single pdf file to the Dean of the Faculty of Economics and Social Sciences, Heidelberg University, Prof. Timo Goeschl, Ph.D. ([jobs@wiso.uni-heidelberg.de](mailto:jobs@wiso.uni-heidelberg.de)) no later than **November 4, 2026**. In the list of publications, please highlight five titles you consider as most representative of your work. Additional documentation, including copies of publications, will be requested from selected candidates, and should not be submitted with the application.

Heidelberg University stands for equal opportunities and diversity. Qualified female candidates are especially invited to apply. Persons with severe disabilities will be given preference if they are equally qualified. Information on job advertisements and the collection of personal data is available at [www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/job-market](https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/job-market).

Postdoctoral Scholar, Research Assistant

(accepting applications)

**Posting end date:** 2 Nov 2026

**Ad text:**

**Position Title: Research Associate (Postdoctoral Scholar) in Wealth Inequality - Stone Center on Socio-Economic Inequality**

**Job ID: 32383**

**Compensation: $90,000/year plus an allowance for research-related expenditures, as well as an allowance for hiring research assistants from the Graduate Center’s student population. This position is generously funded by the James M. and Cathleen D. Stone Foundation.**

**Closing Date: November 2, 2026**

**CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION**

The Graduate Center of the City University of New York (CUNY) is the focal point for advanced teaching and research at CUNY, the nation's largest urban public university. The Graduate Center’s commitment to research and scholarship for the public good is exemplified by its more than 30 centers, institutes, and initiatives, including its Advanced Science Research Center (ASRC), a 200,000 square-foot facility in upper Manhattan, designed to promote collaboration among scientists in five areas of growing importance in serving the community: nanoscience, photonics, structural biology, neuroscience, and environmental sciences.

The Graduate Center (GC) benefits from highly ambitious and diverse students and alumni—who in turn teach hundreds of thousands of undergraduates every year. Through its public programs, the Graduate Center enhances New York City’s intellectual and cultural life.

**STONE CENTER**

The James M. and Cathleen D. Stone Center on Socio-Economic Inequality conducts and promotes quantitative research using inequality as a lens on society, politics, and the economy. The core faculty, the affiliated and postdoctoral scholars, and the students working within the center share a commitment to scholarship that is data-driven, interdisciplinary, and policy-oriented, often addressing questions that are cross-nationally comparative or global in scope.

The Stone Center:

* Is home to a group of six core faculty members (senior scholars) who teach sociology, political science, and economics, and who—with graduate students and external affiliated scholars—are actively engaged in research addressing diverse aspects of socio-economic inequalities;
* Hosts the US Office of LIS, the cross-national data center in Luxembourg, with socio-economic microdata from 60+ countries;
* Organizes public programs related to inequality and collaborates with the Graduate Center’s Office of Public Programs on several large events each year.

For more information about the Stone Center visit <https://stonecenter.gc.cuny.edu/>

**CALL FOR ONE POSTDOCTORAL SCHOLAR**

The Stone Center seeks to hire a Research Associate (Postdoctoral Scholar) working on wealth and/or wealth inequality, to carry out research focused on the United States, on other countries, or through cross-country comparisons. This position reports to the Stone Center Director and is a full-time two-year position beginning in August 2027.

Priority will be given to candidates conducting research in the following areas:

* Distribution of private and public wealth, wealth inequality, wealth concentration;
* Land distribution and inequality;
* Intergroup wealth disparities (e.g., by gender, race, ethnicity, migration status, subnational unit);
* Intersection of wealth inequality, climate policies, and climate crisis:
* Determinants (including public policies) and consequences of wealth concentration;
* The economics of property and ownership rights;
* Wealth taxes, real estate and property taxes, estate/inheritance/gift (EIG) taxes, and/or other policies that shape wealth accumulation and wealth transfers; behavioral responses.

The allocation of time will be approximately as follows:

* 70% - The postdoctoral scholar will have the opportunity to work individually on their own research projects related to wealth.
* 30% -The postdoctoral scholar will join the ongoing team of the GC Wealth Project. The postdoctoral scholar will contribute to the Wealth Project's work, which includes gathering, curating, and producing data and research related to wealth inequality, wealth composition, and wealth taxation, across countries and over time-the precise role will be determined mutually.
* In this role, the postdoctoral scholar will work closely with other Wealth Project team members, including one other postdoctoral scholar, and may also supervise M.A./Ph.D. student research assistants. The work includes collaboration with the GC Wealth Project teams located both in NYC and in the satellite office of the Stone Center on Socio-Economic Inequality at Roma Tre University. The Rome Office is overseen by Salvatore Morelli, the director of the GC Wealth Project.

All full-time and part-time CUNY staff are expected to work in-person at their campus office 80% of their work time. For full-time staff, this is equivalent to 8 out of 10 days of in-person work in a two-week period (e.g., 8 days in person, 2 days remote). This hybrid work schedule is subject to change.

**Minimum Qualifications:**  
Doctoral Degree in a related field and demonstrated research ability.

**Other Qualifications:**

A preferred candidate should have:

* Ph.D. degree in economics, sociology, political science, demography, public policy, or a related social science discipline

-Applicants must have completed their Ph.D. no more than seven years prior to the application date;

-Applicants must demonstrate that their Ph.D. degree will be completed by late-August 2027;

* Research portfolio that demonstrates interest in and experience with empirical, methodological, or theoretical scholarship on socio-economic inequality, with a focus on the content areas noted above;
* High level of technical skill, expertise in a range of quantitative methods, and experience with complex data sets;
* Experience with communicating research findings in a way that is relevant to the public.

**Benefits:**  
CUNY offers a comprehensive benefits package to employees and eligible dependents based on job title and classification. Employees are also offered pension and Tax-Deferred Savings Plans. Part-time employees must meet a weekly or semester work hour criteria to be eligible for health benefits. Health benefits are also extended to retirees who meet the eligibility criteria.

**How to Apply:**

Go to <http://cuny.jobs/> and search for Job ID 32383.

Please click on “Apply Now” below which links to the registration screen. If you are a new user, you must register to apply. If you already have a user ID, please use your existing ID. The following are all required:

1. Curriculum vitae.
2. Statement of interest, not to exceed 1,500 words. The statement of interest should:

-Summarize your qualifications, and describe your past work related to wealth inequality.

-Include a brief description of the projects that you hope/expect to carry out during the two-year period.

-Indicate whether you have a Ph.D. degree and the month and year in which you attained your Ph.D. degree.

-If you do not have a Ph.D. degree at the time of application, please indicate the month and year by which you will have a Ph.D. degree.

3. One writing sample. Please do not submit multiple writing samples.
4. Contact details for three (3) professional references, including their name, title, organization, telephone number, and email address. Letters of recommendation are not required with the initial application.

**Please upload all documents in PDF format as one file.**

The search committee will complete an initial round of screening. Candidates selected for interviews will be asked to provide three letters of recommendation. All interviews will be conducted remotely via Zoom.

Scholars studying facets of economic inequality may choose to apply for a different Stone Center postdoctoral scholar position, referenced here as Job ID 32384. Candidates whose research experience is appropriate for both positions are welcome to apply to both.

A J-1 visa may be offered to eligible individuals.

**Equal Employment Opportunity:**  
CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer.

Assistant Professor of Economics

Location: Syracuse, NY

Pay Range: $120,000 - $160,000

Pay Determination:

Salary offers at Syracuse University will be based on education, experience, and relevant skills, as well as the academic or professional discipline of the position in the context of the home department, school, or college. Salary offers may also be influenced by prior relevant work or industry experience, where applicable. Faculty pay ranges are for 8.5 months' salary unless otherwise specified.

FLSA Status: Exempt

Hours:

As determined by department chair.

Job Type: Full Time

Rank: Assistant

Campus: Syracuse, NY

Unionized Position Code: Not Applicable

Job Description:

The Department of Economics in the Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs at Syracuse University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in econometrics. We seek candidates who combine methodological depth in econometrics with a strong research interest in applied microeconomics (e.g., urban, industrial organization, labor, education, health, or public), applying modern econometric tools to policy-relevant questions.

The Department of Economics has a national reputation for excellence in applied microeconomic research and econometrics, and offers B.A., B.S., M.A., Ph.D., and combined degree programs. It is housed within the Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs, and we seek candidates with interdisciplinary interests. Successful candidates may be invited to affiliate with one of Maxwell's fourteen interdisciplinary research centers and institutes.

Preference will be given to candidates whose work connects well with adjacent areas of behavioral science (e.g. behavioral public policy applied to the domains of health and environment, or experimental economics grounded in applied social psychology). The successful candidate will be expected to teach economics and behavioral science courses.

We particularly welcome candidates who value both teaching and research and demonstrate a commitment to student-centered teaching practices, active learning, inclusive pedagogy, and project-based or experiential approaches to education. DKU is an international intellectual community that values diversity, openness, and creative learning. We welcome outstanding educators from around the world who bring diverse perspectives and experiences to a global learning and research environment, and we particularly encourage applications from individuals from underrepresented groups, including candidates from underrepresented parts of the world. Teaching undergraduate students from diverse international contexts is a core responsibility of all DKU faculty.

Duke Kunshan University is a collaborative partnership among Duke University, Wuhan University, and the Municipality of Kunshan, China ([https://dukekunshan.edu.cn](https://dukekunshan.edu.cn/)). With an acceptance rate below 8%, DKU attracts students representing over 75 countries. In addition to its undergraduate program, DKU offers a select number of master's programs, including the Master of Engineering in Electrical and Computer Engineering, the Master of Science in Global Health, and the Master of Environmental Policy.

The DKU pedagogical model draws on Duke University’s educational experience and resources while reimagining undergraduate education within a small, collaborative campus environment. Similar to leading liberal arts colleges in the United States, DKU emphasizes close faculty–student interaction, interdisciplinary learning, and innovative teaching approaches.

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. or equivalent terminal degree in a relevant field related to the advertised position. Demonstrated excellence or strong potential in teaching and research is required. DKU offers internationally competitive compensation, housing allowance, child education benefits (for applicable faculty positions), and professional development support for teaching faculty.

The search committee also welcomes letters of nomination for potential candidates. Nominations and inquiries may be sent to social-sciences@dukekunshan.edu.cn with the subject line “Faculty Search Social Sciences.”

Priority will be given to applications received by October 12, 2026, although applications will be accepted until the positions are filled.

In order to meet Chinese visa requirements, international (non-Chinese) candidates must, prior to the position start date, have at least two years of full-time work experience in a relevant area after receiving their bachelor’s degree (work experience obtained while studying full-time is not considered). Alternatively, candidates may begin their appointment within 12 months of obtaining their master’s or Ph.D. degree, provided they have not held employment between the degree conferral date and the start of the appointment.

The DKU campus is located in Kunshan, approximately 37 miles west of Shanghai, and is easily accessible via high-speed rail and metro systems.

* **[School of Economics](https://economics.uq.edu.au/)** based at UQ’s [Faculty of Business, Economics and Law (BEL)](https://bel.uq.edu.au/)
* Two full-time (100%) permanent positions available
* Positions can be offered at Academic Level B or C
* *Academic Level B:* Base salary in the range AUD$119,462 - $141,545 + 17% superannuation
* *Academic Level C:* Base salary in the range AUD$145,961 - $168,043 + 17% superannuation
* Based at UQ’s vibrant [St Lucia Campus](https://campuses.uq.edu.au/)

**About This Opportunity**

As a teaching and research academic Lecturer (Level B) or Senior Lecturer (Level C) in one of Australia’s leading economics schools, you will join a vibrant, internationally recognised academic community, committed to teaching excellence and international scholarly recognition in your field.

**For US applicants:** A Lecturer (Level B) is broadly comparable to an Assistant Professor in the US, while a Senior Lecturer (Level C) is a more senior appointment with greater expectations across research, teaching and academic leadership.

Key responsibilities at **Academic Level B (Lecturer)** will include:

**Teaching:**

* Contribute to the development of new programs and course materials in the area of focus, in consultation with program advisors and stakeholders, ensuring courses are engaging, relevant and contemporary.
* Teach across a range of settings and actively contribute to educational practice and innovative curriculum design, including online learning and alternative teaching methods.
* Coordinate courses, prepare and deliver lectures and tutorials, and undertake assessment and marking for undergraduate and postgraduate courses.
* Maintain and improve course quality, informed by evaluation tools, to meet industry and educational standards.
* Provide high-quality support to students, including academic counselling and advice.
* Understand and apply University rules relevant to teaching and learning practice.

**Research:**

* Develop a publication record in world-leading or internationally excellent journals in any field of Economics.
* Work with colleagues and postgraduate students to develop and conduct joint research projects and prepare applications for competitive research funding.
* Contribute to applications for external research funding and actively seek, secure and manage research funding.
* Present at key domestic and international conferences and other leading universities.

**Supervision and Researcher Development:**

* Contribute to the supervision of master’s, honours and higher degree by research students.
* Contribute to the recruitment, selection and onboarding of appropriately qualified employees in accordance with University policies and procedures.
* Work to resolve conflicts and grievances promptly, in accordance with University policies and procedures.

**Citizenship and Service:**

* Actively develop partnerships and strengthen relationships with colleagues, industry, government departments, professional bodies and the wider community.
* Demonstrate leadership of self and others through mentoring and collaboration.
* Efficiently manage allocated internal service roles and processes, including participation in decision-making and service on relevant committees.
* Effectively perform a range of administrative functions as required.
* Provide support to other academic staff as needed, including during absences.
* Consistently demonstrate the UQ values.

In addition to the above, responsibilities at **Academic Level C (Senior Lecturer)** will include:

**Teaching:**

* Build and maintain internal and external education collaborations, and undertake and initiate professional learning in teaching.
* Lead programs, disciplines, plans, courses and/or student cohorts.

**Research:**

* Contribute to the development or delivery of partnerships with research end users and external collaborations that produce high-quality research outputs.
* Successfully build teams and contribute to discipline service, including service on editorial boards.

**Supervision and Researcher Development:**

* Establish a track record of successful supervision outcomes.
* Demonstrate responsible research conduct and lead others in this practice.
* Effectively develop supervisees’ capabilities and skills, and manage researcher development.
* Demonstrate leadership in facilitating engagement opportunities for supervisees.

**Citizenship and Service:**

* Consolidate an established record of internal and external service and make appropriate leadership contributions.

This is a Teaching and Research position. Further information can be found by viewing UQ’s [Criteria for Academic Performance](https://content.app.uq.edu.au/bkbiqrpxuy/documents/academic-performance-criteria-TR.pdf) and our **[Appointment Information Booklet](https://content.app.uq.edu.au/bkbiqrpxuy/positiondescriptions/r-69343_lsl_economics_appointmentbooklet.pdf)**.

**About You**

For Appointment at **Level B (Lecturer)**:

Applicants should hold a PhD in Economics or a directly relevant field by the time of commencement. You will also demonstrate:

* A growing profile in teaching and research in the discipline.
* An active research program and a pipeline of work in progress expected to lead to publications in world-leading and internationally excellent journals in Economics.
* The ability to deliver high-quality teaching at undergraduate, honours and postgraduate levels across a range of settings, including small and large groups.
* The ability to coordinate courses and contribute to the development and ongoing improvement of programs, curricula and course materials in the discipline.
* The ability to supervise honours and higher degree by research students through to successful completion.
* Experience in seeking external research funding, or a clear intention to seek, secure and manage such funding.
* The ability to contribute to internal and external service activities.

For Appointment at **Level C (Senior Lecturer)**:

Applicants should hold a PhD in Economics or a directly relevant field. You will also demonstrate:

* An established profile in teaching and research in the discipline.
* An active research program, a significant track record of publications in world-leading and internationally excellent journals, and a pipeline of work in progress targeting these journals in Economics.
* A strong record of securing and managing external research funding.
* A demonstrated record of high-quality teaching at undergraduate, honours and postgraduate levels across a range of settings, including small and large groups.
* A strong track record of course coordination and contributions to the development and ongoing improvement of programs, curricula and course materials in the discipline.
* A solid record of supervising honours and higher degree by research students through to successful completion.
* A growing record of meaningful contributions to internal service, alongside a strong contribution to external service activities.

**About UQ**

As part of the UQ community, you will have the opportunity to work alongside the brightest minds, who have joined us from all over the world, and within an environment where interdisciplinary collaborations are encouraged. As part of our commitment to excellence in research and professional practice in academic contexts, we are proud to provide our staff with access to world-class facilities and equipment, grant writing support, greater research funding opportunities, and other forms of staff support and development.

The greater [benefits](https://about.uq.edu.au/careers/why-work-uq) of joining the UQ community are broad: from being part of a [Group of Eight](https://go8.edu.au/) university, to recognition of prior service with other Australian universities, up to 26 weeks of paid parental leave, 17.5% annual leave loading, flexible working arrangements, access to exclusive internal-only vacancies, and genuine career progression opportunities via the academic promotions process.

**Interested?**

For more information about this opportunity, please contact **Professor Claudio Mezzetti** via email [c.mezzetti@uq.edu.au](mailto:c.mezzetti@uq.edu.au).

For application inquiries, please reach out to the Talent Acquisition team at [talent@uq.edu.au](mailto:talent@uq.edu.au), stating the job reference number (R-69343) in the subject line.

When you apply, please upload your **resume, cover letter, responses to the ‘About You’ criteria, a job market/research paper, and two written references or letters of recommendation**. Please also ensure you **answer all required application questions.**

**Please apply through our listing on the AEA JOE Network**: **[HERE](https://www.aeaweb.org/joe/listing.php?JOE_ID=111478036)**.

*Please note that applications submitted via email will not be accepted.*

**Other Information**

Pre-employment checks may include: verification of the right to work in Australia, qualifications, criminal history checks. This may also include checks relating to gender-based violence matters or other integrity and conduct requirements.

Relocating from interstate or overseas? We may support you with obtaining employer-sponsored work rights and a relocation support package, however upfront costs will still be expected to be covered. You can find out more about life in [Australia’s Sunshine State here](https://about.uq.edu.au/careers/recruitment-process/relocating-queensland).

We're dedicated to [equity, diversity, and inclusion](https://about.uq.edu.au/careers/equity-diversity-inclusion). We recognise that career pathways and opportunities differ, and encourage applications from candidates who may not meet every criterion but can demonstrate their potential relative to opportunity. We’re also happy to support any accessibility needs throughout the recruitment process. Just let us know how we can help by emailing [talent@uq.edu.au](mailto:talent@uq.edu.au) or calling +61 7 3365 2623.

The position may be filled as a full professor or tenure track assistant professor or tenure track associate professor depending on the candidate’s merits and career stage. Information about our tenure track system: [University of Helsinki tenure track](https://www.helsinki.fi/en/about-us/careers/academic-careers/university-helsinki-tenure-track). The goal of the tenure track is to advance to a permanent professor position.

**Job description**

The appointee is expected to develop high-quality and societally relevant research on the economic and business dimensions of agriculture and food systems. The research profile may focus on, for example, farm-level decision-making and the business management of agricultural enterprises (agribusiness), the measurement and analysis of productivity and efficiency, sustainability transitions in agriculture, the functioning of agricultural and food systems and value chains, or international and development-oriented agricultural economics. The position requires expertise in applied economics and the ability to apply advanced empirical methods, particularly econometrics, in both research and teaching.

The position carries teaching responsibilities in agricultural economics, mainly in the Bachelor’s Programme in Environmental and Agricultural Economics (YMTA), the Bachelor’s Programme in Agricultural Sciences (MAAT), the Master’s Programme in Agricultural, Environmental and Resource Economics (AGERE) and the Liberal Arts and Sciences Programme (LAS). It also involves supervision of bachelor's and master’s theses, and doctoral training in the Doctoral Programme in Multidisciplinary Research in Renewable Natural Resources (RENEW). The appointee is expected to build active research and teaching collaboration within the faculty and with external research organisations such as the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke), Pellervo Economic Research (PTT) and the Finnish Environment Institute (Syke), and to strengthen the research group by securing competitive funding, publishing high-quality research and developing international networks.

The tenure track assistant/associate professor or full professor will have a central role in developing agricultural economics research, teaching and doctoral education, and in strengthening the national and international visibility of the field.

**REQUIREMENTS**

An appointee to the position of assistant professor or associate professor in the tenure track system shall have

- a doctoral degree

- the ability to conduct independent scholarly work

- the teaching skills required for the position

- the ability and motivation to pursue an academic career, as demonstrated by publications and other means

An appointee to the position of professor shall have

- a doctoral degree

- high-level academic qualifications

- experience in leading scientific research

- the ability to provide research-based teaching and supervise dissertations and theses

- evidence of international cooperation in the research field they represent

- academic leadership skills

The degree requirement (doctoral degree) must be met by the end of the application period.

When considering the candidates’ qualifications, attention shall be given to scientific and teaching merits. In addition, the candidates’ leadership and interaction skills, as well as activity in the scientific community and public engagement shall also be taken into account.

Scientific merits include

- scientific publications and other research results of academic value

- success in obtaining external research funding

- international research experience

- other international experience

Teaching merits include

- teaching experience

- pedagogical training

- the ability to produce learning material

- other teaching merits

- a teaching demonstration

- participation in doctoral education

Successfully performing the duties of the position requires good spoken and written proficiency in Finnish or Swedish and satisfactory proficiency in the other national language. If you do not yet speak Finnish or Swedish, we expect you to achieve intermediate language proficiency in either language within a reasonable time after being selected for the position. The University provides support for language learning and time for language studies can be included in annual work plan.

To successfully attend to the duties of the position, the appointee must have good English skills as it includes teaching in an English-language master's programme as well as active participation in international research collaboration.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

We offer an interesting opportunity to work in a diverse research environment. At the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry you will carry out research-based teaching at the highest education level in the field in Finland and have the opportunity to take part in internationally valued, first-class research activities. The position is also an opportunity to develop your own professional skills in a multidisciplinary work community of the faculty. Your work will be supported by the research and teaching staff of the department and the faculty as well as the administrative and technical staff at Viikki campus. Furthermore, the university takes care of your well-being by flexible work arrangements, comprehensive occupational health care and wide-ranging, low-cost UniSport services. Professional development is supported in different ways, i.e. by offering versatile staff training, mentoring etc.

The professor’s gross annual starting salary varies approximately between 85 000 and 98 000 euros and the assistant/associate professor’s starting salary approximately between 66 000 and 82 000 euros, depending on the appointee’s qualifications and experience.

There is a six-month trial period in the position. The appointee is expected to reside in Finland while employed by the University of Helsinki. International staff are supported in relocating to Finland.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Applicants are requested to enclose with their applications a **SINGLE PDF file** that includes the following documents in English:

1) CV

2) A short motivation letter and report on how the applicant intends to develop his or her research and focus his or her activities, if appointed (1-2 pages)

3) Report on the applicant’s research activities (including activities in scientific communities, the acquisition of research funding and international scholarly work) (max. 5 pages)

4) A numbered list of publications

5) A report on pedagogical expertise (see the instructions via the link below under University portfolio – Teaching and supervision)

For more detailed instructions on the application documents, please see

<https://www.helsinki.fi/en/about-us/careers/open-positions/instructions-applicants-teaching-and-research-positions>

Applications with the above attachments must be submitted in a **single PDF file**, which is named: agricultural economics\_lastname\_firstname. Other attachments are not required.

The faculty may request shortlisted applicants to submit 5-10 publications of their choice to be sent to the assessors via the electronic recruitment system after the application deadline. In the case of shortlisted applicants, aptitude evaluation may be used as part of the recruitment process.

External applicants, please submit your application using the University of Helsinki Recruitment System via the **Apply Now** link.

Applicants who have a helsinki.fi username and a valid employment contract, a grant researcher's contract, a visiting researcher's or visiting professor's contract at the University of Helsinki are requested to leave their application by using the **Employee login**.

The University of Helsinki welcomes applicants from a variety of genders and linguistic and cultural backgrounds.

The closing date for applications is **2.11.2026 at 23:59 EET.**

Apply at <https://jobs.helsinki.fi/job/Helsinki-Professor-or-tenure-track-Assistant-Associate-professor-in-Agricultural-economics/1373225157/>

**FURTHER INFORMATION**

· About the position: Department Head Marko Lindroos, marko.lindroos(at)helsinki.fi, tel. +358 2941 58068

**ABOUT US**

**The Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry** is located on the Viikki campus. The mission of the faculty is to promote the sustainable use of renewable natural resources through scientific research and research-based teaching. We focus on agricultural and forest sciences, food and nutrition, microbiology, as well as on economics and management. We cover the full natural resource chain from farm to fork, the entire field of forest sciences from soil chemistry to marketing, as well as the environmental effects of related activities. Graduates from the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry are versatile experts in biosciences and business, able to meet the needs of both the business sector and society at large.  
[www.helsinki.fi/en/faculty-of-agriculture-and-forestry](http://www.helsinki.fi/en/faculty-of-agriculture-and-forestry)

**The Department of Economics and Management** conducts high-quality research and teaching, involving the application of economics, management, marketing and consumption theory, methods and perspectives to address issues associated with the goods and services from our terrestrial and aquatic environments: agricultural areas, food systems, forests and aquatic environments. The department has several international research groups. Our researchers also participate in the teaching and development of doctoral programmes. The Department is also a part of Helsinki Graduate School of Economics (HGSE). <https://www.helsinki.fi/en/faculty-agriculture-and-forestry/research/economics-and-management>

**Ad text:**

The Graduate School of International Studies (l’École supérieure d’études internationales – ESEI) at Université Laval, located in Québec City, Canada, is a centre of excellence in multidisciplinary research and teaching on international issues.

ESEI is currently seeking a faculty member whose research focuses on global inequalities and trade. The successful candidate will hold the Research Chair in Global Inequalities and Trade.

The competition is open to candidates from all disciplines relevant to this field. Applications from economics, law, geography, history, sociology, management, political science, and other relevant disciplines are particularly encouraged.

International trade structures power relations among developed countries, emerging economies, and least developed countries, as well as power dynamics among actors within societies. It has a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of millions of people and on their aspirations for a more equitable world. The Chair’s research will examine the reciprocal relationships between the governance of international economic and diplomatic relations, on the one hand, and inequalities, on the other, in the context of the reconfiguration of the emerging world order.

The Chair’s research may address, but is not limited to, the following issues: the role of financial institutions in addressing global economic inequalities (e.g., sovereign debt restructuring); the links between international aid, export-led growth, and human development; the role of sovereign wealth funds and the financialization of the economy in the unequal distribution of wealth and democratic backsliding; the impact of market opening and multinational corporations on local populations; and the preservation of an inclusive multilateral trading system.

In addition to its research activities, the Chair will develop an innovative teaching program based on simulations of negotiations and coordinated action within international organizations working in the fields of international development and trade (IMF, UNDP, WTO, etc.). These initiatives will raise students’ awareness of the importance of multilateral cooperation in reducing inequalities among countries.

A research advisor will support the Chairholder in developing, planning, and submitting research grant applications, while helping to maximize the Chair’s outreach and knowledge mobilization activities. Funding will also be available to support doctoral scholarships associated with the Chair.

The successful candidate will join the Graduate School of International Studies as a regular faculty member beginning June 1, 2027, and no later than September 1, 2027. The appointment may be made at any academic rank, in accordance with the Collective Agreement between Université Laval and the Syndicat des professeurs et professeures de l’Université Laval (SPUL).

**Duties include :**

• Teaching at the graduate level;

• Supervising graduate students in the context of master’s research papers, master’s theses, and doctoral dissertations;

• Conducting research and publishing on global inequalities and trade;

• Participating in teaching and administrative activities associated with ESEI;

• Performing any other activities provided for under the Collective Agreement between Université Laval and SPUL.

**Selection Criteria :**

• Ability to teach in French within three years of appointment;

• A PhD in a field relevant to global inequalities and trade;

• Applications from doctoral candidates who are nearing completion of their dissertation will be considered, provided that a letter from the department chair confirming the expected date of dissertation submission or defence is included;

• A strong commitment to multi/interdisciplinary research and teaching, demonstrated through academic training, a research program, teaching experience, or collaborations;

• An excellent research record, including publications in peer-reviewed journals considered among the leading journals in the candidate’s field, or demonstrated potential to develop an excellent research record for candidates at an early career stage;

• University-level teaching experience;

• A record of securing research funding from granting agencies in the candidate’s field, or demonstrated potential to obtain such funding in the near future;

• Ability to teach a graduate-level research methods course. Proficiency in mixed methods would be an asset;

• Demonstrated involvement in national and international research networks would be an asset;

• Research experience in the Global South would be an asset.

**Employment Conditions :**

• Regular, full-time position;

• Salary commensurate with recognized experience, with benefits, in accordance with the Collective Agreement between Université Laval and SPUL.

**Applications :**

• Application deadline: October 31, 2026

• Start date: June 1, 2027 (no later than September 1, 2027)

**The application file must include:**

A. A cover letter demonstrating, in particular, the candidate’s commitment to multi/interdisciplinary research and international studies;

B. A curriculum vitae;

C. A document of no more than two pages describing a five-year research chair program;

D. One sample of the candidate’s publications.

Valuing equity, diversity, and excellence, Université Laval is firmly committed to providing all its staff with a work and living environment characterized by an inclusive culture. For Université Laval, diversity is a source of strength, and we encourage qualified individuals of all origins, genders, sexual orientations, gender identities or expressions, as well as individuals with disabilities, to apply.

Université Laval also adheres to an employment equity program for women, members of visible or ethnic minorities, Indigenous peoples, and individuals with disabilities. To this end, all applicants will be invited to complete a confidential self-identification form upon submission of their application.

All applications will be processed confidentially.

**Associate Professor or DTU Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Sustainable Travel Behaviour - DTU Management**

DTU Management is looking for an Associate Professor or Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Sustainable Travel Behaviour to join our Transportation Science Division.

In this position, you will contribute to research and teaching within travel behaviour and sustainable mobility and become part of an internationally recognized research environment with strong links to policymakers, public authorities, and industry.

The position offers a unique platform to conduct pioneering research in Sustainable Travel Behaviour, connected to DTU’s broader ecosystem of technological knowledge and innovation within the transportation sector.

The Transportation Division is an internationally recognized research environment with strong expertise in transport and mobility. Our interdisciplinary team brings together researchers from fields such as engineering, economics, psychology, data science, computer science, mathematics, and statistics.

We deliver ground-breaking fundamental research as well as research-based insights and tools for policymakers and industry. We collaborate closely with research communities in Denmark and abroad, and with Danish authorities. This includes a large ongoing contract with the Ministry of Transport, under which we provide policy support to solve the great challenges in the transport sector. This includes responsibility for the national travel survey.

Human behaviour and its underlying drivers are embedded throughout our research on transport systems and mobility. Our research creates a foundation for policy support related to key challenges in the sector, such as the green transition, mobility for all user groups, congestion and pressured land use both in large cities and rural settings; equity, safety, and risk; and derived negative externalities of transport.

The overarching focus of the position is understanding human mobility and sustainable travel behaviour when planning transportation systems. This should also be seen in a broader context understanding how urban and rural surroundings influence travel behaviour, and based upon this formulating policies and regulations for more sustainable mobility.

**What we offer**  
We offer an international research environment, with a collegial, team-oriented environment in an elite university based in Greater Copenhagen. We have good opportunities for collaboration, supervision and co-supervision of graduate students and attractive teaching conditions.

Denmark offers abundant funding opportunities for leading edge research from its many private and public research foundations in addition to the EU funding schemes. To support the obtaining of funding, DTU and the department provide highly specialized and individual funding support and guidance depending on your needs and where you are in your career.

Furthermore, Denmark is one of the countries in the world with the highest degree of digitalization, and hence researchers have access to unique longitudinal datasets on households, companies, transport behaviour, land use, etc. DTU has a close collaboration with public authorities, which secures both impacts of research and access to surveys, experimental and register data.

The position is full-time and based at DTU Lyngby campus, just north of Copenhagen. Copenhagen is renowned around the world for its relaxed atmosphere, fantastic restaurants, festivities and high quality of life, being number one on the 2025 Global City quality of life index.

* A solid national and international network within and beyond academia
* An ambition to push boundaries and define future research agendas that address societal challenges

**VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT FOR AN ACADEMIC POSITION**

The University of Cyprus, founded in 1989, is committed to research excellence and the continuous development of its undergraduate and graduate programmes. To best serve its research and educational aims, the University recruits high-calibre academic staff who can make significant contributions to the development of internationally- competitive research projects and to the design and delivery of new curricula.

The University is committed to promoting inclusivity, diversity, and equality, as well as the elimination of all forms of discrimination, to provide a fair, safe, and pleasant environment for the entire university community, where students and staff members will feel supported both in their professional and personal development, within and beyond their multiple identities. To this end, the University seeks to create the necessary conditions that will encourage and respect diversity and ensure dignity both in the workplace and society at large. Moreover, the University has adopted specific policies to promote equal opportunities, as well as respect and understanding of diversity, while it is committed to promoting and maintaining a working, teaching, and learning environment, free from any form of discrimination, whether direct or indirect.

**DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMICS**

The University of Cyprus invites applications for **two (2) academic positions at the rank of Lecturer or Assistant Professor** in the Department of Economics. Applications are invited from candidates in **all fields of Economics**.

**The tenure-track system at the University of Cyprus includes two non-tenured ranks: Lecturer (three-year appointment) and Assistant Professor (four-year appointment).**

For both academic ranks, candidates must hold a Doctorate in Economics or in a closely related field from an accredited university.

The minimum requirements for each academic rank are available at <https://rb.gy/e9oi7>. These include, among others, previous academic experience, outstanding research achievements and notable scientific contributions, experience in developing and teaching of high quality undergraduate and graduate curricula.

Candidates do not need to be citizens of the Republic of Cyprus.

The official languages of the University of Cyprus are Greek and Turkish. The languages of instruction in the Department are Greek and English. In case the selected candidate is not proficient in the Greek language, the candidate and the Department shall ensure that the former acquires sufficient knowledge of the Greek language within 3 years from the date of appointment.
