To strengthen our team and join our junior faculty, we are looking for a **Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d)** with a focus on international economics. The position is **for three years** with possible extension for up to six years, based in **Munich, Germany.**

We are seeking a candidate who is committed to high-quality, policy-relevant research and strongly motivated to advance her\*his own research agenda and contribute to the policy debate. The ability and willingness to raise third-party research funding are expected.

Our team investigates how globalization and international trade policy affect firms, workers and economies. Our research covers topics such as the role of trade barriers and trade agreements, global value chains, innovation, and firms’ responses to international shocks. We combine international trade theory with applied econometrics and big data.

**The ifo Institute is one of Europe’s leading economic research institutes**. Research at ifo combines academic excellence with economic policy relevance. Our faculty and postdoctoral researchers publish their work in high-impact journals and use their findings to bring scientific perspectives into policy debates. The scope of our research is broad, covering most fields in economics. Please check out our research activities in-depth on the following webpage: <https://www.ifo.de/en/research>

We promote outstanding research by providing generous administrative and research support, an exceptional data infrastructure, and tailored training and development programs. Our international CESifo research network offers ample opportunities for scientific exchange with top-class scholars. Guest researchers regularly visit the Institute. Thanks to our close cooperation with the University of Munich (LMU), our postdoctoral researchers are integrated into the junior faculty of the Department of Economics at LMU. The position has no formal teaching obligation; however, limited teaching is encouraged.

Our junior faculty members…
---------------------------

### Research

* work on exciting questions in virtually all fields of economics
* regularly publish in top general interest and field journals
* cause impact because they bring scientific findings into policy debates
* contribute to the debate on economic and educational policy in line with our claim "Shaping the Economic Debate"
* are highly demanded on the national and international job market, both in academia and outside, and achieve placements as full or associate professors at top universities

### People

* are part of a team **of about 118** **economists**
* are embedded in a vibrant economics community in Munich
* are part of the Department of Economics at LMU Munich
* can participate in the structured Junior Faculty Development Program and have the opportunity to teach at LMU Munich
* engage with international top-class economists within our CESifo network with over 2,200 members from all over the world

### Support

* have access to an exceptional data infrastructure and other supporting services

### ifo

* have an initial three-year employment contract, with the option to be extended for another three years
* receive their salary according to TV-L E 13 or E 14 (starting at 68,200 EUR incl. special annual payment) depending on publications and are part of the company pension scheme (VBL) (in addition to the statutory pension insurance)
* are supported in their professional and personal development with flexible working hours, the possibility of mobile work and many tailored training and development programs, and are equipped for this in the best possible, modern and comprehensive way
* work in close proximity to the English Garden and the Isar
* can use our beautiful garden, which connects our historic buildings, to relax during lunch breaks, for a coffee in between or to chat with colleagues.
* are entitled to a relocation allowance after passing their probationary period if they move to Munich or the surrounding area from a radius of 200 km or more
* will be supported with German courses if needed

We support the EU Commission's initiative by developing a special human resources strategy for research staff that takes into account the principles of the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. Our membership in the Familienpakt Bayern (Bavarian Family Pact) reinforces our measures to reconcile family and career. We promote professional equality regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual identity. We strive to increase the proportion of women in research and therefore expressly encourage women to apply.

Candidates should hold a PhD in economics or be about to defend a PhD soon. Interested candidates should submit their application via [EJM - Econ Job Market](https://econjobmarket.org/). Applications should include **a cover letter, CV, job market paper,** and at least **three reference letters.**

The deadline for submitting applications is **November 18, 2026**. We will conduct virtual interviews as part of the 2026-2027 European Job Market between **Monday, December 14, 2026 and Thursday, December 17, 2026.** Flyouts will start on **Monday, January 11, 2027**.

Please feel free to contact [jobmarket@ifo.de](mailto:jobmarket@ifo.de) if you have any questions. For further information on careers at the ifo Institute, please visit <https://www.ifo.de/en/career-ifo> .

**Ad text:**

The Utrecht University School of Economics (U.S.E.) invites applications for an Assistant Professor position in Economics. The position is embedded in the Applied Economics section.

**Your job** The Applied Economics section brings together researchers working in a large variety of areas *of applied economics* (e.g. public economics, behavioral economics, health economics, economics of crime, regional/urban economics, development economics, labour economics, economics of education, and other applied fields) with researchers working on the history, methodology, and/or philosophy of economics. Research and teaching in the section is typically empirical, policy-oriented, and sometimes multidisciplinary.

We welcome candidates from any field of applied economics. The position involves teaching in areas where economics is itself the object of study. These areas include the history of economics, economic history, philosophy of economics, and economic/econometric methodology, such as for example the courses “Contemporary Economics in Historical Perspectives” or “Ethical and Historical Reflections”. Candidates should explain in their cover letter how their research connects to these teaching areas.

The position includes 60% teaching time (including 5% governance), and 40% research time.

The candidate’s responsibilities will include:

* conducting high-quality research in economics or a closely related field;
* teaching undergraduate and graduate courses within U.S.E.;
* contributing to courses at U.S.E. in which economics is reflected upon (e.g. history of economic thought, philosophy of economics, economic methodology, or related themes) but also teach at the Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE) programme to which U.S.E. contributes;
* engaging in interdisciplinary collaboration within Utrecht University, for example with the [Descartes Centre](https://www.uu.nl/en/descartes-centre) for the History and Philosophy of the Sciences and the Humanities, a university-wide center that promotes critical reflection on academic disciplines, methods, and the role of knowledge in society.

**Your qualities** The successful candidate is expected to:

* hold a PhD, or be close to finishing their degree, in economics or another field related to the position;
* have a potential for excellence in research, targeting publications in top international peer-reviewed journals;
* be able to inspire students from undergraduate to graduate levels, and prior teaching experience is a plus;
* have excellent communication and management skills;
* have an excellent command of spoken and written English.

Utrecht School of Economics offers Master programs in English and bachelor programs in both English and Dutch. A good command of English is essential. Knowledge of Dutch is an asset. We expect the candidate to learn Dutch and offer support.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming academic environment. We particularly encourage applications from women/non-binary people, members of underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities, and others who would contribute to the diversity and excellence of our academic community.

**Our offer** We offer:

* a position (0.8-1.0 FTE) for 12 months. *After a positive evaluation the position will be made permanent;*
* a full-time monthly gross salary between €4925,- and €6682,- in scale 11 of the Collective Labour Agreement Dutch Universities (CAO);
* 8% holiday bonus and 8.3% end-of-year bonus;
* a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave, and flexible employment conditions based on the Collective Labour Agreement Dutch Universities.

In addition to the [employment conditions](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/working-at-utrecht-university/terms-of-employment) from the CAO for Dutch Universities, Utrecht University has a number of its own arrangements. These include agreements on [professional development](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/working-at-utrecht-university/professional-development), leave arrangements, [sports and cultural schemes](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/working-at-utrecht-university/terms-of-employment/sports-culture-and-it) and you get discounts on software and other IT products. We also give you the opportunity to expand your terms of employment through the Employment Conditions Selection Model. This is how we encourage you to grow.

For more information, please visit [working at Utrecht University](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/working-at-utrecht-university).

**About us** The candidate will become a member of the Applied Economics Section at the Utrecht University School of Economics (U.S.E.). The [Utrecht University School of Economics](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/utrecht-university-school-of-economics-use/about-use) (U.S.E) is part of the Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance at Utrecht University. U.S.E. aims to contribute to an economy where people flourish by taking a broad view on welfare and its causes. We aspire to be an internationally renowned school of economics with scientifically rigorous and socially relevant research and education. We enrich economics with other disciplines to better solve problems and identify opportunities, from a business as well as government perspective.

The [Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/faculty-of-law-economics-and-governance) is a faculty at the heart of society, with a strong focus on social issues. Our subjects of Law, Economics and Governance give us a strong mix of academic disciplines that complement and enhance each other. This is a unique combination and a mark of our faculty's strength.

A better future for everyone. This ambition motivates our scientists in executing their leading research and inspiring teaching. At [Utrecht University](https://www.uu.nl/en), the various disciplines collaborate intensively towards major [strategic themes](https://www.uu.nl/en/research/profile/strategic-themes). Our focus is on Dynamics of Youth, Institutions for Open Societies, Life Sciences and Pathways to Sustainability. [Sharing science, shaping tomorrow](https://youtu.be/yHkvpRYVPiA).

**More information** For more information about this position, please contact Ulrich Zierahn-Weilage at [u.t.zierahn-weilage@uu.nl](mailto:u.t.zierahn-weilage@uu.nl)

**Apply now** As Utrecht University, we want to be a [home](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/equality-diversity-inclusion) for everyone. We value staff with diverse backgrounds, perspectives and identities, including cultural, religious or ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability or age. We strive to create a safe and inclusive environment in which everyone can flourish and contribute.

To apply, please send your curriculum vitae, letter of motivation, job market paper, 2-3 reference letters (or contact details for 2-3 referees), research and teaching statements via the ['apply now'](https://link.inhroffice.com/528d19af-1236-49c5-acfa-5c742e42a504) button.

**Job title**: Assistant / Associate / Full Professors in Economics

**About the role**:

Imperial Business School is seeking qualified applicants for faculty positions in its [Department of Economics and Public Policy](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/faculty-research/academic-areas/economics-public-policy/) at the rank of Assistant, Associate and Full Professor in Economics.

Applicants for the position of Assistant Professor should have the potential to publish innovative, rigorous, and relevant contributions in top academic journals and to develop into excellent teachers. Candidates for an Associate or Full Professor position should demonstrate considerable excellence in research, teaching and service. The appointed candidates will be encouraged to proactively engage in research grant applications; Imperial’s strategy “Science for Humanity” provides significant opportunities for interdisciplinary research.

As with most business schools, most of the department’s teaching focuses on applied economics, management and analytics modules. The first students on our innovative undergraduate degree in Economics, Finance and Data Science finished their studies this summer; our MSc programmes include Economics and Strategy for Business and an interdisciplinary degree in Climate Change, Management and Finance. Our interdisciplinary MSc in AI, Economics and Policy, taught jointly with the Department of Computing, will admit its first students in September 2027.

Applications from women, BAME and other groups who are currently underrepresented in the School are especially welcome. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for neurodiversity and disability associated needs.

The initial interviews will be conducted virtually in December, and fly-outs will be in January/February.

**What you would be doing**:

You will contribute to Imperial’s mission as a leading research-intensive university, developing your own range of research and teaching on our degree programmes. You are encouraged to develop research collaborations within and outside Imperial, and we provide travel funding to facilitate this. You will share in the administrative tasks of running the department and the Business School, to an extent appropriate to your career stage.

**What we are looking for**:

* You will have a PhD in Economics or a related field, or (for an assistant professor) expect to have one before taking up the post
* You will be able to demonstrate capability for high-quality innovative research in your area, with a strong research agenda and pipeline. Applicants for associate or full professor should be developing an international reputation for their research.
* You will have experience (appropriate to your level) in teaching economics to university students.

**Further Information**

These are full-time posts. Associate and Full Professors are offered permanent contracts. Assistant Professors will be offered a seven-year fixed term contract and will be expected to apply for promotion to Associate Professor during their sixth year. Those who are promoted to Associate Professor will receive a permanent contract.

Apply through the Imperial College portal (<https://www.imperial.ac.uk/jobs/>) and search job reference BUS00897, read the full advert, job description and application instructions document and submit the following documents:

· Application form

· CV

· Cover letter that explains your reasons for applying to Imperial

· Research statement

· Teaching statement

· Evidence of teaching scores (where applicable)

· 3 research papers (one paper for current / recent PhD students)

Those applying for an assistant professor post should also ask three referees to email a reference letter to [EPPrecruit@imperial.ac.uk](mailto:EPPrecruit@imperial.ac.uk) by the closing deadline.

If you require any further details on the role, please contact: Professor Richard Green – [r.green@imperial.ac.uk](mailto:r.green@imperial.ac.uk)

**Closing deadline is 03 November 2026**

If you experience any technical issues while applying online, please don't hesitate to email us at [support.jobs@imperial.ac.uk](mailto:support.jobs@imperial.ac.uk). We're here to help.

**Ad text:**

**Full Professor Banking & Finance Utrecht University** Utrecht University School of Economics (U.S.E.) is a young and growing Economics department. The position of the Chair in Banking and Finance contributes to the (inter)national reputation and profile of U.S.E. in line with its multidisciplinary vision on research, teaching, and impact in the area of banking and finance. The Chair plays a crucial role in strengthening the international research profile and expertise of U.S.E. and its Finance section.

**Your Job** The main goal of the Chair in Banking and Finance is to further advance research (aligned with the relevant UU strategic themes, mainly “Institutions for Open Societies” and/or “Pathways to Sustainability”), and education in the relevant fields of expertise. Apart from their own research, we expect the Chair to play a stimulating role in the USE research community; to promote a research environment in line with USE’s aims for Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion; and to attract external research funding through grants and/or consulting. Additional duties include supervision of PhD Candidates and mentoring of (Post-Doctoral) researchers resulting in state-of-the-art PhD-manuscripts and publications, and the transfer of knowledge to society by organizing events (such as conferences and workshops). Teaching of the chair will connect the field with other relevant disciplines, in line with U.S.E.’s Real World Perspective. Cooperation with other USE sections and other departments and faculties within UU in teaching and research is strongly encouraged. The tasks and responsibilities of the Chair will include:

• Performing and encouraging scientific research in the field of Banking and Finance;

• Supervision of PhD students and post-Doctoral researchers;

• Participating in education in the U.S.E. Bachelor and Master programs, as well as executive education;

• Leadership in contributing to the research and teaching climate, including stimulating and supervising multidisciplinary research and teaching;

• Contributing to the financial sustainability of U.S.E., including active participation in external fundraising.

**Your qualities** The person we are looking for is a passionate and creative academic with a strong background in finance and a genuine interest in Banking and Finance. Given the current developments in this field, knowledge/research on digital/data science and AI, and the impact upon Finance – including its role for enabling societal transitions - is highly valued. We expect the chair to have a vision on the impact of data and societal transitions on finance and the financial industry. The person should be able to integrate digital knowledge in courses in the academic Finance master programs.

The ideal candidate for this position has a strong publication record and teaching experience in the field of Banking and/or Finance. The candidate is also willing and able to reach out to researchers active in other fields, such as economics and management. This requires an open and inquisitive mind, and a willingness to experiment and explore new avenues and methods in research and academic teaching. We anticipate that the candidate is willing and able to communicate complex scientific results and insights to an audience of policy makers, societal stakeholders, and the wider public; proven ability in this respect is considered a plus.

The following profile will be expected of the chair holder:

• A doctorate in the field of finance or economics;

• A strong track record in research, as demonstrated among others by publications in internationally recognised journals, a high number of citations, and preferably membership of policy advisor bodies (e.g. CEPR, NBER, etc);

• Impact in the field, as demonstrated by e.g. editorial roles, conference organisation, invited talks or keynote lectures, engagement with policy or professional organisations, or other forms of societal or academic impact;

• An interest in and commitment to multidisciplinary research and collaboration across disciplinary boundaries;

• Significant experience in academic leadership, demonstrated, for example, through leadership roles, the development of teams or research programmes, mentoring and supporting colleagues, or other contributions to an inclusive, socially safe and collaborative academic environment, together with a clear vision on academic leadership;

• Enthusiasm and commitment to the further development of research and teaching in banking and/or Finance from a multidisciplinary perspective within UU;

• Ability to acquire external funding;

• Good communication skills;

• Fluency in English; ability to communicate in Dutch is preferred.

**Our offer**

• an employment contract for 12 months with the prospect of a permanent employment contract;

• a permanent employment contract;

• a working week of 28- 40 hours and a gross monthly salary between € 7.475 and €10.815 in the case of full-time employment (salary scale H2 under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU));

• 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus;

• a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU.

In addition to the terms of employment laid down in the CAO NU, Utrecht University also offers a range of its own schemes for employees. This includes arrangements for professional development, various types of leave, and options for sports and cultural activities. You can also tailor your employment conditions through our Terms of Employment Options Model. In this way, we encourage you to keep investing in your personal and professional development. For more information, please visit Working at Utrecht University.

**About us** A better future for everyone. This ambition motivates our scientists in executing their leading research and inspiring teaching. At Utrecht University, the various disciplines collaborate intensively towards major strategic themes. Our focus is on Dynamics of Youth, Institutions for Open Societies, Life Sciences and Pathways to Sustainability. Sharing science, shaping tomorrow.

The Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance is a faculty at the heart of society, with a strong focus on social issues. Our subjects of Law, Economics and Governance give us a strong mix of academic disciplines that complement and enhance each other. This is a unique combination and a mark of our faculty's strength.

The Utrecht University School of Economics (U.S.E) is part of the Faculty of Law, Economics and Governance at Utrecht University. U.S.E. aims to contribute to an economy where people flourish by taking a broad view on welfare and its causes. We aspire to be an internationally renowned school of economics with scientifically rigorous and socially relevant research and education. We enrich economics with other disciplines to better solve problems and identify opportunities, from a business as well as government perspective.

U.S.E.’s Bachelor’s programme Economics & Business Economics offers students a solid foundation in economic theory and methods, combined with insights from business economics, finance, entrepreneurship, innovation, ethics and sustainability. The programme has about 1,500 students from various backgrounds and nationalities and is taught in English; a Dutch track will be introduced in September 2027.

**More information** For more information about this position, please contact prof. dr. Niels Bosma, Head of Department Utrecht University School of Economics, at [n.s.bosma@uu.nl](mailto:n.s.bosma@uu.nl), or prof. dr. Frank Verbeeten, Head of Section Finance Utrecht University School of Economics, at [f.h.m.verbeeten@uu.nl](mailto:f.h.m.verbeeten@uu.nl).

The structural report for this vacancy contains more information on Utrecht School of Economics and can be requested from Babette Berrocal, [b.p.m.berrocalvargas-vandenbrink@uu.nl](mailto:b.p.m.berrocalvargas-vandenbrink@uu.nl).

First interviews are planned to take place in December 2026.

Candidates for this vacancy will be recruited by Utrecht University.

**Apply now** At Utrecht University, we strive to be a place where everyone feels at home. We value colleagues with different backgrounds, perspectives and identities, including differences in culture, religion or ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability and age. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and contribute. Read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion. If you have any questions about accessibility, for example regarding your workplace Adam Smith Hall, the application process or your work, please contact us via our HR contact page.

A valid Certificate of Conduct (VOG) is required for this position. This will be requested as part of the application process.

Knowledge security screening can be part of the selection procedures of academic staff. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology.

University of Victoria - Department of Economics - Solid Carbon Project
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Application Review**: Begins 15 January 2027; the position remains open until filled

**Overview**
------------

The Department of Economics at the University of Victoria (UVic) invites applications for a Postdoctoral Fellow to work on the economics and policy of geological carbon storage and capture, as part of the UVic and Ocean Networks Canada Solid Carbon project. The Fellow will work under the supervision of Dr. Felix Pretis and as a member of the interdisciplinary Solid Carbon team.

The position combines project research with independent research. The Fellow will deliver research outputs for the Solid Carbon project, and will also have protected time to develop their own research agenda in carbon storage, carbon dioxide removal, and climate policy.

**About the Solid Carbon Project**
----------------------------------

Solid Carbon is investigating how carbon dioxide can be permanently and safely stored as rock in the basalt beneath the seafloor off the west coast of Vancouver Island. The project is funded through the Government of Canada’s New Frontiers in Research Fund (Transformation stream) and brings together researchers in the social sciences, geosciences, ocean sciences and engineering. Its work includes ongoing research, public engagement and consultation with coastal and Indigenous communities, and a small-scale demonstration project.

The economics team studies the costs, risks, incentives and policy frameworks that will determine whether geological carbon storage can be deployed at scale. More information: [solidcarbon.ca](https://solidcarbon.ca).

**The Role**
------------

The Fellow will contribute economic research to the Solid Carbon project while developing their own research agenda. The project work can be shaped around the Fellow’s expertise and interests. Central economic questions for the project include:

* the costs of geological carbon storage, and how these costs are likely to evolve;
* policy design for carbon storage and removal, including carbon pricing and a carbon takeback obligation compared with alternative instruments;
* the economic impacts and feasibility of scaling up carbon storage.

The Fellow is encouraged to pursue independent research related to carbon storage, carbon removal or climate policy, and to publish in leading field and general-interest journals.

The Fellow will present at project meetings and academic conferences, and may take part in mentoring students working with the team. There may also be opportunities to gain teaching experience in the Department of Economics.

Qualifications
--------------

### **Required**

* A PhD in Economics, Agricultural and Resource Economics, Environmental Science/Studies, Geography, or a related discipline; awarded within the past five years (applicants close to completion are welcome to apply; exceptions to the five-year limit are possible for career interruptions such as parental leave or illness).
* A demonstrated interest in carbon storage, carbon removal, or the economics and policy surrounding them.
* A record of, or clear potential for, high-quality independent research.
* Strong quantitative and empirical skills.
* The ability to work in an interdisciplinary team alongside engineers and natural scientists, and to communicate results to non-economists.

### **Desirable**

* Experience with econometric or empirical methods applied to energy, environmental or climate questions.
* Familiarity with carbon markets, climate policy instruments, or energy and resource economics.
* Experience working with project-level, firm-level or policy data.
* Interest in engaging with policymakers, industry and communities.

### **What We Offer**

* Mentorship and collaboration with the Solid Carbon team.
* Connections to Ocean Networks Canada and the wider Solid Carbon network, and to the Oxford Climate Econometrics project.
* Protected time for independent research and support for career development.
* Research and conference travel funding may be available through the Solid Carbon project.
* Extended health and dental benefits, an employee and family assistance program, and paid sick leave.
* University top-up of Employment Insurance during maternity, parental or adoption leave.
* Office space in the Department of Economics and access to UVic’s library, computing and research facilities.
* A collegial department in Victoria, a mid-sized city on Vancouver Island with a mild climate and easy access to the ocean and mountains.
* Start date: Summer 2027 with some flexibility.

**How to Apply**
----------------

Apply through Econjobmarket. Please submit:

* **Cover letter** (maximum [2] pages) that clearly explains your interest in and alignment with the research goals of the position, in particular carbon storage, and describes what you would contribute to the Solid Carbon project and the independent research you would pursue. Please also indicate if you are a Canadian citizen/permanent resident.
* **Curriculum vitae.**
* **Two to three research papers** (published papers or working papers; a job market paper is welcome - submit any of your research papers under `job market paper' if you do not have a dedicated job market paper).
* **Three letters of reference**, submitted directly by your referees through EconJobMarket.

**Optional**:

* You may submit a video summary of one of your research papers (e.g. job market paper)

Review of applications will begin on **15 January 2027** and continue until the position is filled. We expect to hold online interviews in late January to March 2027. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Questions about the position can be sent to Dr. Felix Pretis at [fpretis@uvic.ca](mailto:fpretis@uvic.ca).

International applicants are welcome. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in Canada by the start date; UVic’s immigration consultant may be able to support international candidates with work permits.

*McMaster University is located on the traditional territories of the Haudenosaunee and Mississauga Nations and, within the lands protected by the Dish with One Spoon wampum agreement.*

Position Description

The DeGroote School of Business at McMaster University invites applications for a tenure-track teaching position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Finance and Business Economics Area. The position will begin on July 1, 2027.

The primary responsibility of the successful candidate will be to teach a variety of courses at undergraduate and master's levels, including large sections of Introduction to Finance as well as trading and investments courses in the undergraduate, MBA, and Master of Finance programs. The candidate will also be involved in the school’s trading floor for which professional trading expertise and experience working with large financial databases is preferable. The teaching requirement is normally eight sections per academic year. In addition, the successful candidate will be expected to emphasize experiential learning, keep abreast of developments in the discipline, participate in the ongoing development of curricula, serve on internal committees, and support the School’s initiatives within the business, academic, and other external communities. Conducting pedagogical research is encouraged.

Candidates must have a doctoral degree in Finance or Financial Economics from an accredited institution (by the time the appointment starts) and should present evidence of teaching excellence and a strong commitment to innovation in teaching. Candidates who hold professional designations (e.g. CFA), have experience teaching large classes, are proficient with financial data platforms such as Bloomberg and Refinitiv’s Workspace, or have professional experience, are preferred.

The Finance and Business Economics Area, the largest of eight Areas comprising the DeGroote School of Business, is committed to excellence in both research and teaching. The School offers a number of programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The Finance and Business Economics Area participates in these programs in several ways, and mounts MBA specializations in Finance and Strategic Business Valuation, a Master of Finance program, and a Ph.D. field in Finance. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the academic programs at both of the School's Hamilton and neighbouring Burlington locations. Further information about the School can be found at <http://www.degroote.mcmaster.ca/>.

Commitment to Inclusive Excellence

The diversity of our workforce is at the core of our innovation and creativity and strengthens our research and teaching excellence. In keeping with its Statement on Building an Inclusive Community with a Shared Purpose, McMaster University strives to embody the values of respect, collaboration, and diversity, and has a strong commitment to employment equity. The University seeks qualified candidates who share our commitment to equity and inclusion, who will contribute to the diversification of ideas and perspectives, and especially welcomes applications from First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples, members of racialized communities (“visible minorities”), persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.

We invite all applicants to complete a brief Diversity Survey, which takes approximately two minutes to complete. All questions are voluntary, with an option to decline to answer. All information collected is confidential and will be used to support efforts to broaden the diversity of the applicant pool and to promote a fair, equitable and inclusive talent acquisition process. Inquiries about the Diversity Survey may be directed to [hr.empequity@mcmaster.ca](mailto:hr.empequity@mcmaster.ca).

Job applicants requiring accommodation to participate in the hiring process should contact the Office of the Dean of Business at [dsbeo@mcmaster.ca](mailto:dsbeo@mcmaster.ca) to communicate accommodation needs.

Dr. Amir Akbari, Chair, Finance and Business Economics Area, DeGroote School of Business, McMaster University, 1280 Main Street West, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada L8S 4M4.

Please submit the following materials:

* A letter of application together with a curriculum vitae describing the impact that career interruptions have had on productivity, if applicable (including a statement regarding Canadian citizenship/permanent resident status (see below))
* A teaching dossier that includes a statement of teaching interests and philosophy, and evidence of teaching experience (breadth, depth, and effectiveness of teaching)
* A brief statement describing any contributions made or planned in relation to advancing equity, diversity and inclusion or inclusive excellence in teaching, research, or service within higher education, community-based or other professional settings (2-page maximum)
* A statement of any research interests in pedagogy and/or the field of finance (optional)
* Three to five letters of recommendation, to be submitted directly by your referees to the e-mail address [dsbfbe@mcmaster.ca](mailto:dsbfbe@mcmaster.ca), with comments from referees on your:
  + demonstrated ability to successfully teach courses at different levels,
  + ability to work in a collaborative and interdisciplinary environment, and
  + contributions to university and/or community service.

Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. All applicants will receive an online confirmation of receipt of their application; however, only short-listed applicants will be contacted for interviews.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority.

To comply with the Government of Canada’s reporting requirements, the University is obliged to gather information about applicants’ status as either Permanent Residents of Canada or Canadian citizens. Applicants need not identify their country of origin or current citizenship; however, all applications must include one of the following statements:

* Yes, I am a citizen or permanent resident of Canada
* No, I am not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada

Pay Transparency Statement

Applicants must have earned a PhD degree in Economics by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, specializing in macroeconomics or a related field, with a demonstrated record of excellence in teaching. We are seeking well-trained PhD economists committed to rigorous research and passionate about central banking. The Bank of Canada has a vision to be “a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada.” No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very centre of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in an environment where we are reinventing central banking, renewing ways of doing business and reinforcing a culture of innovation.

Find out more about the Bank’s current [research priorities](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/research/#priorities), explore the broad range of [staff research](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/research/research-staff/) that our [people](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/research/#people) have the intellectual freedom to pursue, and learn about the ways in which the Bank [supports and collaborates](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/research/#collaborate) with the external research community.

· cover letter

· curriculum vitae

· research paper(s) or job market paper

Subject to the needs and interests of the Bank and the employee, senior economists or senior analysts may move to other Bank departments to pursue research of relevance in new or needed areas. * Develop leading-edge research ideas, produce and disseminate high-quality research papers on Bank priorities

* Collaborate with researchers and policy staff within the Bank, and colleagues from other organizations on multi-disciplinary projects

*McMaster University is located on the traditional territories of the Haudenosaunee and Mississauga Nations and, within the lands protected by the Dish with One Spoon wampum agreement.*

Position Description

The DeGroote School of Business at McMaster University invites applications for a tenured research faculty position in the Finance and Business Economics Area at the rank of Associate or Full Professor. The position will begin on July 1, 2027. The successful candidate will hold the CIBC Chair in Financial Markets. The appointment to the Chair will be for an initial period of five years, with the possibility of renewal for additional terms.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to all aspects of academic activities, including research, teaching, and service. In particular, the successful candidate will contribute to research and scholarship through publishing in high-quality journals in financial economics, participating in prominent national and international academic conferences, actively pursuing research grants, promoting research collaboration, and supervising students in their areas of expertise. The successful candidate will also be expected to contribute to the School's academic programs at both its Hamilton and neighbouring Burlington locations, and support the School’s initiatives within the business, academic and other external communities.

The minimum requirements for the position include:

(i) a Ph.D. in Finance, Financial Economics, or other finance-related field from a reputable institution;

(ii) evidence of a strong scholarly record including publications in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and acquisition of research funding; and

(iii) a demonstrated commitment to teaching excellence and supervision of graduate students.

The Finance and Business Economics Area, the largest of eight Areas comprising the DeGroote School of Business, is committed to excellence in both research and teaching. The School offers a number of programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The Finance and Business Economics Area participates in these programs in several ways, and mounts MBA specializations in Finance and Strategic Business Valuation, a Master of Finance program, and a Ph.D. field in Finance. Further information about the School can be found at <http://www.degroote.mcmaster.ca/>.

Commitment to Inclusive Excellence

The diversity of our workforce is at the core of our innovation and creativity and strengthens our research and teaching excellence. In keeping with its Statement on Building an Inclusive Community with a Shared Purpose, McMaster University strives to embody the values of respect, collaboration, and diversity, and has a strong commitment to employment equity. The University seeks qualified candidates who share our commitment to equity and inclusion, who will contribute to the diversification of ideas and perspectives, and especially welcomes applications from First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples, members of racialized communities ("visible minorities"), persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.

We invite all applicants to complete a brief Diversity Survey, which takes approximately two minutes to complete. All questions are voluntary, with an option to decline to answer. All information collected is confidential and will be used to support efforts to broaden the diversity of the applicant pool and to promote a fair, equitable and inclusive talent acquisition process. Inquiries about the Diversity Survey may be directed to [hr.empequity@mcmaster.ca](mailto:hr.empequity@mcmaster.ca).

Job applicants requiring accommodation to participate in the hiring process should contact the Office of the Dean of Business at [dsbeo@mcmaster.ca](mailto:dsbeo@mcmaster.ca) to communicate accommodation needs.

How to Apply

Please apply online via the McMaster Academic Careers website: <https://hr.mcmaster.ca/careers/current-opportunities>, (Faculty Postings, Job #78694), addressing your application documents to:

Dr. Amir Akbari, Chair, Finance and Business Economics Area, DeGroote School of Business, McMaster University, 1280 Main Street West, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada L8S 4M4.

Please submit the following materials:

* Letter of application together with a Curriculum Vitae describing the impact that career interruptions have had on research productivity, if applicable (including a statement regarding Canadian citizenship/permanent resident status (see below))
* Research statement including a selection of research work (published articles and/or working papers)
* Statement of teaching interests and philosophy (including evidence of teaching effectiveness and supervision of graduate students)
* Brief statement describing any contributions made or planned in relation to advancing equity, diversity and inclusion or inclusive excellence in teaching, research or service within higher education, community-based or other professional settings (2-page maximum)
* Names of at least three referees. Letters of reference are not required and will not be reviewed at the application stage. The Area will request letters of recommendation from referees at later stages of the search process.

Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. All applicants will receive an on-line confirmation of receipt of their application; however, only short-listed applicants will be contacted for interviews.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority.

To comply with the Government of Canada’s reporting requirements, the University is obliged to gather information about applicants’ status as either Permanent Residents of Canada or Canadian citizens. Applicants need not identify their country of origin or current citizenship; however, all applications must include one of the following statements:

* Yes, I am a citizen or permanent resident of Canada.
* No, I am not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada.

Pay Transparency Statement

The starting salary will not be less than $116,663, and will be determined based on rank, discipline, experience, and qualifications. Salaries for faculty members progress through a Career Progress/Merit Plan; average salaries by rank and Faculty for previous academic years can be found here.

Postdoctoral Fellow Positions in Platform Economics and Data-Driven Market Design, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen)

**Position Introduction**
-------------------------

We are seeking multiple highly motivated postdoctoral researchers to join an interdisciplinary team collaborating closely with a leading global ride-hailing platform.

A key strength of this collaboration is close partnership with the platform in designing and executing large-scale randomized controlled trials to evaluate marketplace interventions in real-world settings. Researchers also have access to exceptionally rich, high-resolution proprietary data, supporting rigorous causal inference, empirical analysis, and high-fidelity modeling and simulation of marketplace dynamics at scale.

Ongoing and planned research topics span information design, the use of generative artificial intelligence in marketplace decision-making, and the effects of pricing, incentives, and dispatch algorithms on participant behavior and market outcomes. The research program also involves multiple large-scale, platform-wide field experiments across several of these areas.

We welcome applicants with strong backgrounds in causal inference, structural estimation, advanced machine learning, and simulation. We are especially interested in scholars eager to apply cutting-edge methods to real-world data to uncover insights that are both academically rigorous and practically actionable. The overarching goal is to inform the design of smarter, more equitable, and more efficient platform ecosystems.

The position will be formally affiliated with the School of Management and Economics at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen). The postdocs will be supervised by [Prof. Yiming Zhang](https://sme.cuhk.edu.cn/en/teacher/1826) of CUHK-Shenzhen. The research team includes the following faculty from other institutions: [Prof. Qiuping Yu (Georgetown),](https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/0031Q00002bhQFrQAM/qiuping-yu) [Prof. Yong-Pin Zhou](https://foster.uw.edu/faculty-research/directory/yong-pin-zhou/) (University of Washington), [Prof. Yunan Ji](https://www.yunanji.com/) (Georgetown), and our current postdoc and research assistants.

Since 2018, our research team has maintained a close collaboration with this ride-hailing platform. Our prior work has focused on the design and optimization of virtual queuing systems, combining large-scale randomized field experiments with structural modeling to generate actionable insights. Research from this partnership has been published in *Management Science* and received multiple awards, including the MSOM Service Management SIG Best Paper Award, INFORMS Service Science Best Paper Award, and the CSAMSE Best Practice Award. Notably, our recommended strategies were adopted platform-wide and led to an 80% improvement in customer experience.

**Research Team**
-----------------

● [Prof. Yiming Zhang](https://sme.cuhk.edu.cn/en/teacher/1826) is an Assistant Professor of Operations Management at the School of Management and Economics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. His research focuses on platform operations. He has extensive collaboration experience with platform firms including the ride-sharing, food delivery, and logistics platforms. His work has been published in *Management Science* and has received several best paper awards.

● [Prof. Qiuping Yu](https://gufaculty360.georgetown.edu/s/contact/0031Q00002bhQFrQAM/qiuping-yu) is an Associate Professor of Operations Management and Business Analytics at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business. She is also an associate editor for the *Manufacturing & Service Operations Management (MSOM)* journal. Her research explores how digital and service platforms can improveoperational efficiency and equity by harnessing real-world behavioral data from both consumers and workers. She employs a range of methods—including large-scale field experiments, structural modeling, and machine learning—to generate actionable insights on platform design, labor scheduling, and fairness across sectors such as ride-sharing, retail, restaurants, customer service, and law enforcement. Her work has been published in leading academic and practitioner outlets, including *Management Science*, *MSOM*, *Harvard Business Review*, and *Brookings Research Briefs in Economic Policy*, and has been featured in major media such as *The Wall Street Journal* and *Bloomberg Businessweek*.

● [Prof. Yunan Ji](https://www.yunanji.com/) is an Assistant Professor of Strategy at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business. Her research lies in the intersection of industrial organization and public economics, with a focus on health care markets. Her work has been published in the *Quarterly Journal of Economics, PNAS,* among others.

● [Prof. Yong-Pin Zhou](https://foster.uw.edu/faculty-research/directory/yong-pin-zhou/) is a Professor of Operations Management at the Foster School of Business, University ofWashington. His research interests lie in the analytical modeling and data analysis of service systems, with a recent focus on digital platforms. His work has been published in leading journals including *Management Science*, *Operations Research*, *Marketing Science*, and *Manufacturing & Service Operations Management*. He is a recipient of the NSF CAREER Award and multiple best paper awards.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

1. A Ph.D. (obtained or soon to be obtained) in Economics, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field.

2. Strong training in econometrics and machine learning; proficient programming skills in Python, R, Stata, MATLAB, or similar tools.

3. Demonstrated ability or strong potential for publishing research in top-tier academic journals on topics related to platform economy, behavioral decision-making, empirical industrial organization, applied microeconomics, and/or operations research/management.

4. Good communication skills and previous experience collaborating with industry is a plus.

**Position Details.**
---------------------

**Job Position:** Post Doc Fellows.

**Duration:** Two years.

**Location:** Beijing (on-site at the collaborating company)

**Start Date:** As early as is mutually agreeable. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**Primary Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

1. Conduct collaborative research within the scope of the project.

2. Facilitate communication and coordination with the science, engineering and product teams at the ride-sharing platform.

3. Disseminate research findings through academic publications, conferences, and policy engagements.

**Salary and Fringe Benefits**
------------------------------

The annual salary for this position ranges from RMB 470,000 to 580,000 (approximately USD 66,000 to 80,000), commensurate with the candidate’s experience and accomplishments. Employee benefits will be provided according to the relevant labor laws of Mainland China as well as CUHK-Shenzhen regulations.

**Application Procedure**
-------------------------

Interested applicants should submit:

1. Cover letter detailing background and interest.

2. Curriculum vitae.

3. Published and/or working papers (if applicable).

4. Two letters of recommendation.

Applications and inquiries should be sent to Prof. Yiming Zhang at [zhangyiming@cuhk.edu.cn.](mailto:zhangyiming@cuhk.edu.cn) Please include**“PostdocApplication–[Your Name]”** in the email subject line. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until positions are filled.

The Faculty of Economics and Management of Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg in cooperation with the Halle Institute for Economic Research (IWH) seeks to fill **two positions** at the rank of **Assistant Professor (W1) in** ***Financial Economics.***

We look for candidates with strong teaching and broadly defined research profiles in Financial Economics that bear the potential for academic excellence. A focus on **Labor and Finance**, **Financial Intermediation,** or **Corporate Finance** is particularly useful. Applicants are expected to employ rigorous quantitative methods and state-of-the-art empirical approaches. Experience with the latest AI methods is desirable and a keen interest to apply economic research to policy questions is advantageous.

The Assistant Professorships strengthen the collaboration between the University and the IWH, which is one of the seven economic research institutes of the Leibniz Association ([www.iwh-halle.de](https://www.iwh-halle.de/en)). The IWH focuses on research in financial and labor markets as well as productivity growth and innovation. The Assistant Professorships shall strengthen the joint research focus in Finance of the IWH and the Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. The successful candidates will join IWH’s Department of Laws, Regulations and Factor Markets and the Financial Markets Department, respectively.

The requirements for the positions are: the completion of a PhD in Economics or Finance by summer of 2027 at the latest, the potential for successful publications in leading international journals, and ideally an emerging network of international research collaborations. The successful candidates are expected to teach in the Faculty’s Bachelor and Masters Programmes and in the PhD program of IWH-DPE. While knowledge of German is desirable, it is not a requirement for the positions.

The employees are assigned the status of civil servants with limited tenure (*Beamtenverhältnis auf Zeit*). The contract will initially be limited to three years, and may be extended by a further three years given a positive evaluation.

The School of Public Policy at the University of Maryland, College Park seeks to appoint a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Science and Technology Policy, starting in Fall 2027. The successful candidate will strengthen the School’s research and teaching capacity at the intersection of science, technology, and public policy and contribute to the continued development of science and technology policy as a strategic area of focus for the School.

We seek candidates with an ambitious research agenda focused on how public policy shapes the development, deployment, and governance of science and technology and how scientific and technological change affects international relations, governments, markets, institutions, risk management and society. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, science and innovation policy; research and development policy; semiconductor and industrial policy; standards and regulation; emerging technology governance; cybersecurity; biotechnology; space policy; quantum technologies; international, national, and homeland security; energy and climate technologies; international competition and cooperation in science and technology; and the institutions and processes through which scientific and technical expertise informs policymaking.

Candidates should demonstrate the potential to develop a strong record of high-quality scholarly research, effective teaching, policy and public engagement, and institutional service. The successful candidate will have the potential to develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program; teach in the School’s undergraduate and graduate programs, including the development of foundational courses in science and technology policy as well as advanced courses in their areas of expertise; and contribute to collaborations across the School and the University, such as the School’s Center for Governance of Technology and Systems, the Global Policy Institute, the Center for Global Sustainability, Center for International and Security Studies at Maryland, the Do Good Institute, and other units across UMD, including the Artificial Intelligence Interdisciplinary Institute at Maryland (AIM).

PhD or equivalent terminal degree in public policy, natural or physical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, information science, economics, political science, international relations, sociology, or another relevant field by the time of appointment.

Assistant Professor in Empirical Microeconomics (tenure track)

The Dean of the Faculty of Economics and Administration, Masaryk University ([ECON MUNI](https://www.econ.muni.cz/en)), invites applications for a tenure track position of Assistant Professor in Empirical Microeconomics at the [Department of Economics](https://www.econ.muni.cz/en/about-us/organizational-structure/561100-deptof-economics):

We are looking for a candidate who:

* Holds a PhD in Economics or a closely related field and has an established international research network.
* Has research experience in empirical microeconomics, particularly in labour economics, behavioral economics, or public economics.
* Demonstrates a strong publication record or outstanding research potential, evidenced by a high-quality job market paper.
* Has excellent quantitative and empirical research skills.
* Is highly motivated, independent, and capable of developing and pursuing an ambitious research agenda.

What does the position entail:

* Conducting high-quality research, publishing in leading academic journals, and presenting at international conferences.
* Developing and submitting national and international research grant proposals.
* Collaborating on ongoing research projects and contributing to the Department's research activities.
* Teaching in English with a reduced teaching load (approximately 30 teaching hours per semester).
* Supervising master's theses and PhD students.

What do we offer:

* A full-time (40 hours per week) Assistant Professor position at Masaryk University, one of the leading research universities in Central and Eastern Europe.
* An initial three-year contract with the possibility of extension. Contract renewal and eligibility for tenure are subject to satisfactory performance reviews and a successful external evaluation.
* A flexible starting date, preferably September 1, 2027.
* A gross monthly salary of EUR 2,500–3,500, depending on involvement in research projects.
* Relocation assistance and dedicated support from the [MUNI Welcome Office](https://www.muni.cz/en/about-us/careers/international-employees).
* A friendly, collaborative, and international research environment.
* Opportunities for professional development, including research seminars, international exchanges, research visits, and participation in collaborative projects.
* Flexible working hours and occasional remote work to support work–life balance.
* A comprehensive benefits package, including eight weeks of paid annual leave, meal and pension contributions, language courses, discounted mobile plans, sports activities, and vaccinations.
* The opportunity to live and work in [Brno, a vibrant university city](https://www.brnoregion.com/Work) with excellent connections to Prague and Vienna.

About the workplace

[Masaryk University](https://youtu.be/nZGsNs3nGm0) is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment to its 35,000 students and 5,500 employees.

MUNI is located in the university city of [Brno](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9kal6NSc_Nc), Czech Republic. Based on the most recent OECD Better Life Index data, the Czech Republic ranks next to the US and the UK. Proximity to nature and other historical cities (e.g., Prague, Vienna, Budapest), variety of cultural and entertainment attractions, and top personal safety make Brno one of the top 100 university cities in the world according to students.

ECON MUNI research groups conduct quality research in empirical economics with focus on topics ranging from labour economics (esp. migration, and discrimination) and behavioral economics.

[Members of the empirical microeconomics research group](https://www.econ.muni.cz/en/about-us/organizational-structure/561100-deptof-economics) conduct research with peers from other Czech, European, and American universities. Members of the faculty have published in journals such as Journal of Public Economics, Journal of Urban Economics, Journal of Economic Behaviour and Organization, Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, Scientific Reports, European Economic Review or Public Choice. Empirical research group extensively cooperates with [experimental](https://mueel.econ.muni.cz/) and [health economics](https://hepii.econ.muni.cz/en) research groups.

Application and selection procedure:

The application shall be submitted online by January 31, 2027 (11:59 p.m., CET) via an e-application (Please, use the link in the e-Application section below). Interviews for the position will be held online or in-person at Masaryk University. Online and in-person interviews may be scheduled on a rolling basis and early applications are encouraged.

The candidate shall provide the following:

* cover letter with a description of your research agenda in the desired area,
* a full professional Curriculum Vitae including the complete bibliography of published works (or provide a link where the information could be found),
* job market paper and/or up to two other research papers,
* names, e-mail addresses, and phone numbers of 3 references; references will be contacted independently to submit reference letters

After submitting your application successfully, you will receive an automatic confirmation e-mail from jobs.muni.cz.

For further information about the position and the department, please contact Ondřej Krčál, at [ondrej.krcal@econ.muni.cz](mailto:ondrej.krcal@econ.muni.cz) Please do not send applications directly by e-mail.

If you need help uploading your application or have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact the head of HR department Dominika Tvarožková, e-mail: Dominika.Tvarozkova@econ.muni.cz

All interested candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of personal background. The selection process is based on an Open Transparent Merit-based Recruitment Policy. Masaryk University does not discriminate in educational or employment opportunities or decisions on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or sexual orientation. The faculty holds the HR Excellence Award.

We are looking forward to hearing from you!

Prof. Mgr. Jiří Špalek, Ph.D.

**Ad text:**

The Kiel Institute for the World Economy invites applications for the 2027 cohort of its Albert O. Hirschman Postdoc Program, offering one- or two-year postdoctoral appointments starting on 1 September 2027.

The program honors Albert O. Hirschman – who was born in Berlin, fled Nazi Germany, and became an eminent scholar in international economics, development economics, geoeconomics and international political economy. Hirschman valued creativity over conformity and left a lasting mark on economics and the social sciences. In his spirit, the program brings together exceptional early-career economists who are eager to pursue bold, relevant questions in international economics and help shape the future of the field.

**Program overview**

The program is highly selective and admits multiple postdoctoral participants per year, aiming to build a small, cohesive cohort. Participants can choose to work in our offices in Berlin or Kiel, embedded in the Kiel Institute's research environment and broader policy network. We expect participants to pursue independent research at the highest international standards, to engage with our seminar culture, and to contribute – by choice and fit – to collaborative projects.

The program focuses on international economics broadly defined, including fields such as international trade, international finance, macroeconomics, development, climate economics, as well as geoeconomics, security and defense, and the economics of conflict.

Contracts will be offered for one or two years, depending on the job market outcome. A one-year appointment is intended for candidates who plan to accept a subsequent position (for example, an Assistant Professorship). A two-year appointment is intended for candidates without a confirmed follow-up position.

**Career development**

Career development is a central feature of the program. Each participant will have one or more professors of the Kiel Institute as mentors and a small "peer board" of senior scholars (including external professors) for strategy and placement advice.

The program organizes structured job-market preparation for participants joining for two years, including paper polishing, application materials, mock interviews and talks, and targeted placement mentoring. Participants may also receive tailored grant-writing training with one-to-one feedback on proposals.

**Your profile**

To be eligible, applicants must hold a PhD in economics or a closely related field that was awarded within the three years preceding the program start or must have formally submitted their dissertation by 1 September 2027 (with the defense shortly thereafter). Strong written and spoken English is required; German is not required.

We seek candidates with excellent research potential in international economics (trade, finance, macroeconomics, development, climate, or geoeconomics). Applicants should demonstrate the ability to conduct high-quality independent research, as evidenced by a strong job market paper and/or clear potential to publish in leading academic journals, and a clear, feasible research plan with policy relevance.

Successful candidates will be based in Berlin or Kiel and take part in the Institute's regular research activities.

We particularly welcome applications from researchers working on geoeconomics, security and defense, or conflict, and aim to admit at least 50% women to the program. Eligibility is open to all nationalities; the Institute supports visa and work-permit procedures.

**We are offering**

Participants control their own budget to hire research assistants, for conference travel, research stays abroad, or to run a seminar series or mini workshop with external speakers. Teaching and administrative duties are kept to a minimum, but we offer teaching practice opportunities at partner universities, as well as participation in selected ASP training courses to learn state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the group receives financing and support to present and network at major Kiel–CEPR conferences – such as those on China, Africa, Geoeconomics, and the Kiel Trade Summit – which offer direct exposure to top scholars and policymakers.

Postdocs will earn a gross annual salary approximately in the €56k–€79k range, depending on experience and qualification, with a German TV-L E13 (100%) contract with full social security coverage, including health insurance. Participants benefit from travel and research support and from a family-friendly environment including paid parental leave in line with German law (with contracts extended for the duration of parental leave). Office space, IT support, and access to Institute data resources are provided at the host location.

The Kiel Institute for the World Economy values diversity. We welcome applications regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion/belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. The Kiel Institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy. We promote the professional opportunities of women and strongly encourage them to apply. Women with equivalent qualifications, competence and expertise will be given preference. We are committed to employing persons with recognized disabilities and will therefore give them preference over persons without disabilities if they are equally qualified.

**How to apply**

Applications for the 2027 intake are due **30 November 2026 (23:59 CET)**, with decisions by mid-January 2027. Application photos should not be included.

Please apply via EconJobMarket and submit the following documents online:

* A CV
* A cover letter stating your preferred host location (Berlin or Kiel) and naming one or two potential mentors at the Kiel Institute
* A research statement
* A job market paper or comparable writing sample
* Two or three confidential letters of reference, submitted directly by the referees
* Applications must be complete, and the proposed research must be anchored in economics.

For selection, we place special attention on research excellence and the potential for field-leading contributions, as well as the clarity, feasibility, and relevance of the research agenda.

Interviews will be conducted remotely by video starting December, 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview with potential mentors.

**Contact**

Head of the program: Prof. Dr. Julian Hinz ([Julian.Hinz@kielinstitut.de](mailto:Julian.Hinz@kielinstitut.de)).

The Kiel Institute for the World Economy seeks applications for a full-time **PostDoc position in quantitative economics**. The position is part of a new Leibniz-funded transfer project on AI and structural economic models for economic policy.

**Your Role**

Your main role is to produce high-quality research. You will work with structural economic models in fields such as international trade, macroeconomics, finance, public, spatial or climate economics, apply them to current policy questions, and help assess how reliable AI-assisted model analysis is. You will work closely with policy partners. Beyond the project, you will have freedom and support to pursue your own research agenda toward publication in leading journals.

**Your Profile**

The Institute of Economics and Econometrics at the University of Geneva (Switzerland) invites applications for two postdoctoral positions in environmental and agricultural economics, starting in Spring or Summer 2027.

The positions are part of a research programme examining the effects of supply-chain policies aimed at reducing deforestation, with a particular focus on how international trade and national policies affect land-use change, as well as an emphasis on causal inference using remote sensing data.

**Position 1:** Deforestation and Land Use, or Agricultural Insurance (Open Research Agenda)

The successful candidate will design a research project related to deforestation and land use, or to agricultural insurance, using tools from fields such as:

- trade models, particularly quantitative spatial and trade models;  
- dynamic discrete choice models, particularly land-use decision models;  
- econometrics, particularly machine learning methods applied to remote sensing data;

The Research Department at Statistics Norway invites applications for a two-year fixed-term postdoctoral position in economics, funded by the Research Council of Norway through "[Match effects and matchmaking in education](https://leuven.economists.nl/matched/)" (MatchEd, project no. 358940). The position is based in Oslo, Norway, with an anticipated starting date of September 1, 2027.

The Research Department conducts economic research using extensive Norwegian administrative data. The department has an established group of researchers working in applied microeconomics, including the economics of education, and close connections with the University of Oslo and the international research community.

### About the project

MatchEd explores how the assignment of students to schools, programs, and tracks affects academic outcomes, motivation, and equality of opportunity. Beyond estimating whether some schools or programs benefit particular students more than others (match effects), the project aims to identify the mechanisms behind this heterogeneity and to translate these insights into evidence-based guidance for designing fairer and more effective assignment systems. The project exploits centralized admission systems (e.g., deferred acceptance with priority-based cutoffs) linked to population-wide registers.

The project is led by [Edwin Leuven](https://leuven.economists.nl/) (Statistics Norway and the University of Oslo) and [Sturla Løkken](https://sites.google.com/site/sturlalokken) (Statistics Norway).

### Job description

The successful candidate will conduct empirical research using Norwegian administrative data and collaborate with other project members on research papers intended for publication in international economics journals. The position provides opportunities to pursue original research within the scope of the project, with no teaching obligations.

### Qualifications

Applicants will be evaluated primarily on research potential, the quality of their research, and the relevance of their interests to the project.

Candidates should have:

* A PhD in economics or a closely related field, completed by the starting date. Candidates who expect to complete their PhD before taking up the position are welcome to apply.
* Strong training in applied microeconometrics, particularly causal inference.
* Experience working with and analyzing individual-level microdata.
* The ability to conduct independent research and collaborate effectively with other researchers.
* Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of Norwegian is not required.

Prior research in the economics of education is an advantage but is not required.

### What we offer

* A two-year fixed-term position as Researcher/Postdoctoral Researcher (position code 1109), with a salary in the range NOK 675 000 – 780 000 per year, depending on qualifications. A higher salary may be considered for particularly well-qualified applicants.
* Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund ([SPK](https://www.spk.no/en/)) and access to Norway’s comprehensive social insurance system and public services.
* Full-time research position with no teaching obligations.
* Research funds for travel and conference participation.
* Flexible working conditions.
* A stimulating and collegial research environment with opportunities for professional development.
