**VISITING OR TERM PROFESSOR**

The Hadley Van Vliet Professorship in Agricultural Economics

**Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics**

**University of Saskatchewan**

Formal applications are invited from qualified individuals for the *Hadley* *Van Vliet Term Professorship in Agricultural Economics* in the **Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics** at the **University of Saskatchewan** in Canada**.** The position has an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027, or soon thereafter. This is a term position with a mutually agreed upon duration of between 1 to 5 years. The position includes generous research support to help the successful candidate develop and advance their research program.

The successful candidate will have a Ph.D. in Agricultural Economics or Economics or closely related field and demonstrated potential for research excellence in areas of importance for Saskatchewan agriculture. The specific research area is open, but candidates who most closely match the objectives of the Hadley Van Vliet Professorship are preferred. These objectives are:

1. To analyze and address pressing issues in agriculture, particularly those relevant to Saskatchewan agriculture;
2. To engage with students and colleagues through the ideas, understanding and analysis that can be applied to major issues in agricultural economics;
3. To engage and communicate research findings to agriculture stakeholders; and
4. To work with public institutions and their agencies in seeking solutions to agricultural and rural issues.

The successful candidate will:

1. Develop an innovative research program in agricultural and/or international economics.
2. Teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, strengthening their analytical skills and understanding of the agricultural economy.
3. Communicate effectively with a wide range of industry stakeholders.
4. Rigorously analyze agricultural issues and communicate findings to diverse audiences.

Along with high-quality research, the successful candidate will deliver up to 2 courses per year in either undergraduate or graduate instruction in areas that align with candidate qualifications and department needs (the specific courses will be determined at the time of appointment). The successful candidate will provide leadership and mentorship to both graduate and undergraduate students and is also expected to engage with relevant agricultural industry stakeholders.

We welcome applications from scholars at all career stages. Past holders of the Hadley Van Vliet Professorship have included both recent PhD graduates and established academics. The Department is committed to supporting the professional and scholarly development of the successful candidate, including providing strong mentorship to early-career scholars. Past early-career holders of the Professorship have gone on to successful tenure-track academic careers.

**The Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics** has a long history of research excellence in agricultural economics, policy and agribusiness. The department offers both a Ph.D. and M.Sc. in agricultural economics, as well as undergraduate programs in agribusiness, agricultural economics, and renewable resource management. The department is situated within the **College of Agriculture and Bioresources,** recognized as an international leader in applied research and scholarship with expertise in, and integrated across, four primary themes: Food, Feed and Bioproducts; Environment and Ecology; Business and Applied Economics; Plants and Animals. The college has a century-long reputation for teaching, research, and outreach and has been a consistent strength both for the university and the region. The college continues to play a pivotal role in the development of agricultural and food industries in Saskatchewan, building on a legacy of public engagement and cooperative partnerships. Our departmental faculty are committed to providing exceptional learning experiences and preparing graduates for leadership roles in the global bio-economy.

The University of Saskatchewan is situated on Treaty 6 Territory and the Homeland of the Métis. The main campus is in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, a fast-growing metropolitan area with a diverse and thriving economic base, supporting a vibrant arts community and a full range of leisure opportunities. Overall, the University has a long-standing reputation for excellence in teaching, research and scholarly activities, offering a full range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs to a diverse student population of over 25,000.

Salary bands for this position for the 2026 – 2027 academic year are as follows: Assistant Professor: $113,527 to $135,535; Associate Professor: $135,535 to $157,543; Full Professor: $157,543 to $183,219. Additional research funding for the Professorship is included to assist the appointee in developing and continuing a productive research program.

This position is supported by a comprehensive benefits package which includes a dental, health and extended vision care plan; pension plan, life insurance (compulsory and voluntary), academic long-term disability, sick leave, travel insurance, death benefits, an employee assistance program, a professional expense allowance, and a flexible health and wellness spending program.

The University is committed to employment equity. Members of Designated Groups (women, indigenous people, people with disabilities and visible minorities) are encouraged to self-identify on their applications.

**A GLOBAL FIRM WITH A CURIOSITY-DRIVEN CULTURE**

As the global asset management business of Prudential, we’re solving financial challenges for millions of people around the world. To do that we need top talent, which we attract by fostering a truly collaborative culture in which everyone is encouraged to *keep asking*. We seek clarity and insight at all stages, from delving into individual security characteristics to understanding our clients’ investment goals at the broadest level.

If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!

**What you will do**

PGIM’s Strategic Capital Group (SCG) is responsible for providing institutional clients with asset-liability management, portfolio strategy, and asset allocation solutions harnessing PGIM’s multi-asset expertise across public and private credit. SCG oversees liability-aware portfolio construction and strategic asset design on behalf of its clients, while also partnering with other teams including PGIM Credit and PGIM Real Estate to deliver best-in-class private origination, credit underwriting, investment research, and risk management capabilities across a full range of asset classes. SCG is the investment manager for Prismic, a reinsurance platform launched by Prudential together with other strategic investors.

This position is within the Portfolio Analytics team of SCG and will assume key responsibilities in the growth of our state-of-the-art quant platform for dynamic portfolio optimization based on rigorous asset-liability simulation and economic scenario generation. You will focus, in particular, on modeling the dynamics of diverse asset classes as well as underlying economic risk factors, which will feed into real portfolio construction projects, both for live deals and in-force business, not just post-allocation diagnostics.

You will be based in our Newark, NJ office and will follow a hybrid schedule (3 days in-office).

**What you can expect**

* Build stochastic models to enhance and extend our proprietary real-world economic scenario generator
* Contribute to macro-factor and asset-level models that set key parameters within the scenario generator
* Develop advanced techniques to analyze emerging asset classes with sparse historical data
* Develop methodology and tools for attributing changes in asset-liability metrics to underlying risk factors
* Investigate and apply the latest quantitative and AI-based methods to concrete investment-strategy problems
* Work with teams across PGIM to properly model investment strategies across a range of public, private, and structured asset classes for use within our asset-liability simulations

**What you will bring**

* Economics or Finance Ph.D., advanced degree from a quantitative finance program, or comparable academic experience within a quantitative discipline
* Solid programming background, including Python (pandas, numpy, scipy) and exposure to modern transformer technology and foundation models
* Reliable knowledge of core quant finance topics: probability theory, statistics, stochastic models, options theory, yield curve construction, fixed income analytics, CAPM, etc.—both at the technical level but also conceptually, in terms of basic financial intuitions accessible to non-quants

**What will set you apart**

* Familiarity with structured products, private credit, real estate debt, and private equity, as well as previous exposure to insurance liabilities and asset-liability management concepts
* Knowledge about the theoretical foundations of quant finance and about macroeconomic frameworks
* Creativity, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to break down quantitative ideas for non-quant audiences

**\*PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply.**

For instance, our former Fellows obtained faculty positions here at NYU, University of Cambridge, American University, and Johns Hopkins University to list just the most recent ones.

Given the prestigious nature of the position, we offer a generous compensation package which may include NYU faculty housing as well as funds to support research and travel.

The Center for Data Science (CDS) is New York University’s focal point for university-wide efforts in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. The Center was established in 2013 to advance NYU’s goal of creating a world-leading training and research facility serving researchers, industry professionals, and students at the forefront of Data Science, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence. As of 2026, CDS became a department in the newly-formed Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science. Today, CDS counts 28 jointly appointed interdisciplinary faculty and 4 clinical faculty housed on three floors of our modern 60 5th Avenue building, one of New York City’s historic properties. It is home to a top-ranked MS in Data Science program, one of the first PhD programs in Data Science, and an undergraduate program in Data Science, as well as a lively Fellow and Postdoctoral program. It has over 90 associate and affiliate faculty from 25 departments in 9 schools and units. With cross-disciplinary research and innovative educational programs, CDS is shaping the fields of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.

The CDS Faculty Fellow will be expected to work at the boundaries between computational methods and domain sciences. They are also encouraged to develop collaborations with faculty at CDS and NYU. They will lead original research projects of their choosing with impact in one or more scientific domains and in one or more methodological domains (machine learning, computer science, statistics, and applied mathematics). Fellows will also teach courses for CDS students.

We seek outstanding interdisciplinary researchers doing CDS-aligned work in the following areas:

* Core Machine Learning/AI Methods
* Machine Learning Theory
* AI for Science
* Computational Social and Political Sciences
* Responsible AI

Successful candidates will bring a research agenda that can take advantage of the unique intellectual opportunities afforded by NYU, and will have experience in working with researchers across different fields.

This is a full-time, non-tenure position, with a teaching load of one (1) CDS course per year as the primary instructor. You will also be expected to participate in service activities of the Center for Data Science (such as helping review admissions applications, committee work, etc.). Appointments will be for two years. Fellows will be offered a competitive salary and benefits, with funds to support research and travel. A start date of September 1, 2027 is planned.

The Department of Economics and Finance (<https://www.uoguelph.ca/economics/>) is a research-intensive academic unit consisting of 30 faculty members, and offers a range of academic programs leading to the degrees: BA, BComm, MA, and PhD. The University of Guelph is the third largest employer in Guelph, a city of over 144,000 people, located about an hour's drive west of Toronto, Ontario. University of Guelph is a top-ranked comprehensive university in Canada with an enrolment of more than 30,000 undergraduate and graduate students across more than 40 academic units. The University is known for its commitment to student learning, innovative research, and collaboration with world-class partners. It is a unique place, with transformative research and teaching and a distinctive campus culture. People who learn and work here are shaped and inspired by a shared purpose: To Improve Life. Reflecting that shared purpose in every experience connected to our university positions us to create positive change, here and around the world. Our University community shares a profound sense of social responsibility, a drive for international development, and an obligation to address global issues.

Interested applicants should submit: a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching, statements of teaching (including student evaluations), service and research, and samples of research work. Applicants must also arrange for three confidential letters of reference to be uploaded directly by their referees. We will start reviewing applications immediately. The deadline to apply for this position is December 1, 2026, or until a suitable candidate is found.

IÉSEG School of Management invites applications for an **18-month, fully funded postdoctoral position** in Economics, with a focus on economic preferences, subjective beliefs, and decision-making under uncertainty. The appointment is conditionally renewable and is expected to begin in **January 2027**. The selected candidate will be based on IÉSEG’s Lille campus and join the Department of Economics and Quantitative Methods.

ABOUT THE POSITION
------------------

The postdoctoral researcher will join iRisk, the IÉSEG Research Center on Risk and Uncertainty (**iRisk**), and work directly with Professors Loïc Berger and Thomas Epper. The successful candidate will take a leading role in transforming a rich and extensive body of data generated through a Horizon Europe project into high-quality academic publications. The position offers substantial scope for intellectual contribution: developing research questions, shaping analytical strategies, interpreting findings, and leading or co-authoring papers for international journals. It provides an excellent opportunity to build a strong publication pipeline, develop collaborations within an international research network, and establish a distinctive research profile using a unique and already well-developed empirical resource.

The project examines economic preferences, subjective beliefs, and decision-making under uncertainty in the context of climate and environmental policy. The available data offer scope for several distinct but related papers, and the selected candidate will help define and implement the corresponding research agenda.

The researcher will be expected to take substantial ownership of individual papers: identifying promising research questions, developing empirical strategies, carrying out the analyses, interpreting the results, and leading the writing. The position is therefore particularly suited to someone who can work independently, write clearly, and bring several projects from initial analysis to completed manuscripts.

The candidate will work closely with Professors Berger and Epper and with other members of the iRisk team in Lille and Paris. They will receive regular feedback and have opportunities to present the research at conferences and interact with an international network of scholars working on risk and uncertainty, behavioral and experimental economics, decision theory, and applied Bayesian statistics.

Candidates should hold a PhD in Economics or a closely related field or expect to complete it before taking up the position and should be fully fluent in English. Strong empirical skills and experience managing and analyzing complex datasets are essential. Evidence of independent research and academic writing will be an important selection criterion. Relevant expertise in at least one of the following areas is expected:

· Behavioral or experimental economics, preferably with a focus on decision-making under uncertainty, intertemporal choice, or social choice

· Decision-making under risk and uncertainty, particularly the empirical measurement and analysis of preferences and beliefs;

· Applied Bayesian statistics, preferably including experience with hierarchical modelling and simulation methods

We are looking for candidates who embody our core values of **A**ccomplishment, **R**esponsibility, **I**ntegrity, **S**olidarity, and **E**ngagement and who will contribute to our diverse and international community, which includes people of 50 nationalities.

IÉSEG places a strong value on diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from candidates of all backgrounds. Members of groups that remain underrepresented in academia—notably women, minority ethnic groups, LGBTQIA+ people, people with visible or non-visible disabilities, and people from lower socioeconomic backgrounds or economically developing countries—are particularly encouraged to apply.

ABOUT THE iRISK RESEARCH CENTER
-------------------------------

The IÉSEG Research Center on Risk and Uncertainty (iRisk) brings together researchers studying decision-making under risk and uncertainty. Its research ranges from theoretical work on risk and ambiguity to applications in areas such as environmental and climate policy, health, insurance, savings, and portfolio choice.

The successful candidate will join an active research community comprising faculty members, postdoctoral researchers, and doctoral students based in Lille and Paris. Further information about the center and its members is available on the [iRisk website](https://irisk.ieseg.fr/).

ABOUT IÉSEG SCHOOL OF MANAGEMENT
--------------------------------

IÉSEG holds the **“triple crown”** of international accreditations (AACSB, AMBA & EQUIS) and is a member of the “Conférence des Grandes Écoles”. The school offers Bachelor, Master, and Post-Graduate Degrees as well as Executive Education programs. IÉSEG is also one of the leading French business schools in terms of research. The IÉSEG Research Center is **accredited by the French CNRS** (National Center for Scientific Research). Our Lille Campus is in the heart of Northern France (within the triangle made up by London, Paris and Brussels), and our Paris Campus is located in the biggest European business district of “La Défense”. More information on the school can be found here: [www.ieseg.fr/en](http://www.ieseg.fr/en)

WORKING AT IÉSEG
----------------

The selected candidate is expected to begin the position in January 2027 at the earliest. The initial appointment is for 18 months and is conditionally renewable. The gross salary is competitive with those offered by comparable European research and academic institutions. The researcher will be based at IÉSEG School of Management’s Lille campus.

At IÉSEG, we are committed to providing a supportive and engaging work environment. To new faculty members (and their partner), we offer a wide range of resources to help them integrate into the country, culture and school, such as individualized French language courses, a relocation allowance, and housing search assistance. Moreover, all faculty members have access to a competitive salary, as well as benefits such as French social security, a complementary health insurance, meal vouchers, a profit-sharing plan, and a contributory pension scheme. Finally, the school actively promotes research, provides resources for active scholars (e.g., funding conferences and data collection) and offers competitive financial bonuses for high-quality international peer-reviewed research publications.

JOIN IÉSEG!
-----------

Apply by filling out the application form available at: <https://recruitment.ieseg.fr/jobs/8466068-postdoctoral-position-in-behavioral-economics-climate-economics-and-decision-making-under?promotion=2287175-trackable-share-link-econjobmarket>

When applying, please upload a **single pdf file** merging the following documents:

• An updated CV

• The names, affiliations, and email addresses of three references

• A cover letter explaining your motivation to work at the iRisk Research Center and how your experience prepares you for the position

• Two representative (working) papers

For questions about the position, please contact [permanentfaculty.recruitment@ieseg.fr](mailto:permanentfaculty.recruitment@ieseg.fr) / [l.berger@ieseg.fr](mailto:l.berger@ieseg.fr)

**About the University and the New Center**

[Shiv Nadar University Chennai](https://www.snuchennai.edu.in/), an initiative of the [Shiv Nadar Foundation](https://www.shivnadarfoundation.org/), is committed to building a research-oriented, multidisciplinary academic environment with a strong emphasis on excellence in research and teaching. The University is undertaking a **major academic renewal and expansion in Economics and Data Science**. Its existing Department of Economics has laid the foundation for undergraduate Economics education at SNU Chennai. Building on this foundation, the University is establishing the **Center for Economic Analysis and Applied Data Science (CEADS)** to develop a vibrant academic community dedicated to high-quality research, excellent teaching, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

CEADS aims to bring together scholars pursuing ambitious, independent research agendas across Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, and Data Science. The Center seeks to foster original scholarship, active engagement with the international research community, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.

**The University is committed to providing an excellent environment for both research and teaching.** Teaching loads will be comparable to those at leading private universities in India, with responsibilities structured to allow faculty sufficient time to pursue sustained research. Excellence in teaching and high-quality research will both be recognized and valued. The University is also committed to providing institutional support for scholarly activities.

1. **B.S. (Honors) Economics with Minor in Data Science**
2. **B.S. (Honors) Data Science with Minor in Economics**

A third, selective **B.S. (Honors with Research)** pathway will be available to eligible students pursuing either major, offering opportunities for advanced study and supervised research.

Students will follow a common curriculum during the first two years before choosing their major. The programs integrate rigorous economic reasoning with mathematics, statistics, computing, and modern data science, with applications in business, finance, technology, and public policy.

· **Microeconomic Theory, Game Theory, Industrial Organization, and Digital Markets**

· **Macroeconomics, Financial Economics, and International Finance**

· **Statistics, Statistical Learning, Machine Learning, and Computational Economics**

These areas reflect the Center's initial academic priorities. Outstanding candidates in closely related fields are also encouraged to apply.

For **Associate Professor and Professor** positions, applicants should have an established record of high-quality research, demonstrated excellence in teaching, and the capacity to contribute to academic leadership and institution-building.

The University seeks faculty who are committed to pursuing active research programs while maintaining high standards of teaching, student mentoring, and academic responsibility.

The position is a three-year postdoctoral position at the Department of Economics, Econometrics and Finance, funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) project Evaluation of Policy Interventions on Societal Inequality.

**Who are you?**

You are someone with:

* A PhD in economics, econometrics, statistics, or a related quantitative field.

**Ad text:**

**OVERVIEW**

Harvard University’s [Opportunity Insights](https://opportunityinsights.org/) (OI), is seeking applicants for a **Data Scientist.**

Opportunity Insights (OI) is a nonpartisan research and policy institute focused on improving economic opportunity. Founded in 2018, Opportunity Insight has become a nationally- and internationally- recognized leader in the science of economic mobility and in the use of large administrative data to understand and address inequality. Opportunity Insights has published seminal work on national trends in [upward mobility](https://opportunityinsights.org/national_trends/); [racial disparities](https://opportunityinsights.org/race/); the role of [neighborhoods](https://opportunityinsights.org/neighborhoods/), [social](https://opportunityinsights.org/paper/social-capital-i-measurement-and-associations-with-economic-mobility/) [capital](https://opportunityinsights.org/paper/social-capital-ii-determinants-of-economic-connectedness/), and [higher education](https://opportunityinsights.org/education/) in upward mobility; the use of private-sector data to understand disparate impacts in the [recent economic recession and recovery](https://opportunityinsights.org/paper/tracker/); and [new methods](https://opportunityinsights.org/paper/digital-twins/) to estimate program impacts. To complement this research, Opportunity Insights has developed data resources including the [Opportunity Atlas](https://www.opportunityatlas.org/), the [Social Capital Atlas](https://socialcapital.org/), and the [Economic Tracker](https://tracktherecovery.org/) to support evidence-based policy and practice. To date, OI’s work has shaped policy discussions at the national and local level, with nearly a dozen of its studies covered on the front pages of [major media outlets](https://opportunityinsights.org/press/), such as the [*New York Times*](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/03/19/upshot/race-class-white-and-black-men.html), [*The Economist*](https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2022/08/01/a-new-study-shows-how-much-social-capital-matters?utm_medium=cpc.adword.pd&utm_source=google&utm_campaign=a.22brand_pmax&utm_content=conversion.direct-response.anonymous&gclid=CjwKCAjwi8iXBhBeEiwAKbUofStZW26tnaQZXhQcFVjirdne1M5ovu1C9jsRigIagY9V0ZurA4ECNBoCBaAQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds), the [*Wall Street Journal*](https://www.wsj.com/articles/when-the-safety-net-pays-for-itself-11563800405), and have been widely cited in policy discussions, including the President’s State of the Union address.

The **Data Scientist** will have two responsibilities. The first is to conduct economic and statistical analysis to support evidence-based investments and cost-benefit evaluation to promote economic mobility. The person in this role will design and implement statistical and econometric models to estimate program impacts, develop financial models of returns to program investments, and conduct cost-benefit and impact analyses. The second objective is to translate findings from these analyses and other ongoing research at Opportunity Insights into actionable insights for external stakeholders and the broader public, ranging from policymakers to students participating in OI’s new data science courses. Both sets of activities will be conducted in collaboration with other current members of the Opportunity Insights team.

**Term**: This is a two-year term position with a strong possibility of renewal.

**Location**: The position is located in Cambridge, MA, with the possibility of hybrid work arrangements.

**Compensation and Benefits:** Harvard’s salary grades and ranges can be found [here](https://hr.harvard.edu/salary-ranges#ranges). This position is classified at level 59. We invite you to visit Harvard's Total Rewards website [here](https://hr.harvard.edu/benefits-wellbeing) to learn more about Harvard’s benefits package.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The individual taking on this role will be responsible for the following:

**Policy Evaluation and Financial Modeling**

* Lead efforts to acquire, clean, and manage large administrative and program datasets.
* Design and conduct econometric studies assessing the effectiveness of public policies, social programs, and other mobility-related interventions.
* Apply causal inference methods including matching estimators, quasi-experimental designs, and other techniques.
* Model financial returns from alternative portfolios of investments, including expected returns and risk assessment.
* Ensure methodological rigor and transparency in all analyses.

**Cost-Benefit Analysis and Tool Development**

* Conduct cost-benefit analyses (CBA) to estimate returns of programs.
* Quantify direct and indirect economic and social benefits.
* Develop a calculator to estimate cost savings and impacts of state and federal tax revenues.
* Integrate findings into dashboards, reports, and visualizations for internal decision-makers and external partners.

**Teaching and Mentoring**

* Support OI initiatives to teach data science and OI research to high school and college students.
* Supervise and collaborate with junior analysts and predoctoral research assistants as needed.
* Provide technical guidance on modeling, interpretation, and quality assurance.
* Contribute to internal capacity building and knowledge-sharing across teams.

**Communication of Results**

* Produce technical reports summarizing results for relevant internal and external stakeholders.
* Help prepare non-technical policy briefs, reports, and presentations summarizing key findings, uncertainties, and implications.
* Represent the organization in briefings, conferences, and stakeholder meetings.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Background/experience**

* Ph.D. in Economics, Public Policy, Statistics, or related field.
* Minimum 2 years of professional experience in applied econometric analysis, preferably in policy evaluation, government, or academic settings.

**Specific job skills and Competencies**

Expertise in:

* Causal inference and econometric modeling
* Analysis of big data
* Cost-benefit analysis
* Quantitative impact evaluation and forecasting
* Writing technical and non-technical economics papers
* Programming languages such as R, Stata, Python, and SAS

Proven ability to translate technical results into actionable policy insights.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to non-technical audiences.

Experience and interest in working in collaborative settings with other team members.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Please apply through [Harvard’s online portal](https://us.smrtr.io/5phYD). **To be considered for this position, a cover letter and resume/CV must be submitted.** A skills assessment may be required as part of the interview process.

Should you have questions, please contact [hiring@opportunityinsights.org](mailto:hiring@opportunityinsights.org).

**Your colleagues:** You will join one of our three sections, in a department with a vibrant research environment.

**Employment conditions and benefits**

We offer you an internationally oriented and varied job in an enthusiastic team, with excellent working conditions in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU).

The starting date of this position is **1 September 2027** and you will be based at Campus Woudestein, Burgemeester Oudlaan 50 in Rotterdam. This position is open for 1.0 fte. **About: Erasmus University Rotterdam**

Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) is an internationally oriented university with a strong social orientation in its education and research, as expressed in our mission ‘Creating positive societal impact’. EUR is home to 4.100 academics and professionals and almost 33.000 students from more than 140 countries. Everything we do, we do under the credo The Erasmian Way – Making Minds Matter. We’re global citizens, connecting, entrepreneurial, open-minded, and socially involved. These Erasmian Values function as our internal compass and create EUR’s distinctive and recognizable profile. From these values, with a broad perspective and with an eye for diversity, different backgrounds and opinions, our employees work closely together to solve societal challenges from the dynamic and cosmopolitan city of Rotterdam. Thanks to the high quality and positive societal impact of our research and education, EUR can compete with the top European universities. [www.eur.nl](http://www.eur.nl/).

**About: Erasmus School of Economics**

Erasmus School of Economics (ESE) is a leading school in economics in the Netherlands. It has a strong international reputation and aims to do outstanding research. Moreover, it provides excellent education at the BA., MA. and Ph.D. levels. Much research at Erasmus School of Economics is policy relevant, has social impact, and offers a strong research culture, ample research resources, and comparatively low teaching loads.

**About: Applied Economics**

The Department of Applied Economics works on economic questions that matter for society. We aim for world-leading research that firms, consumers and governments can use. Our researchers are affiliated with the Tinbergen Institute, one of Europe's leading research institutes and graduate schools in economics, econometrics and finance. They are also affiliated with the Erasmus Research Institute of Management (ERIM), where we work with colleagues from Rotterdam School of Management (RSM).

Our department has three sections:

**Behavioural Economics** – We study how people make decisions under risk and uncertainty, over time, and in social settings. We want to understand what shapes behaviour, and we design interventions that help people make better decisions. Topics include health behaviour, financial decisions, security, and unethical behaviour such as lying and cheating. We combine decision theory with field, laboratory and online experiments.

**Health Economics** – We are one of the larger groups of health economists at a school of economics in Europe. Our main topics are health inequality, health behaviour, global health, social science genetics, and various topics at the intersection of health and labour economics. Most of our work is empirical, often using quasi-experimental methods and linked administrative data on the Dutch population.

**Strategy Economics** – We do theory-based empirical research on the organisation of firms, industries and markets. Our fields include applied industrial organisation, entrepreneurship, innovation, and regional and urban economics. The section sits at the intersection of economics and business studies, and targets top journals in both economics and management. Our staff also carry out studies for policy makers and industry.

There are many links between the three sections. We particularly, but not exclusively, welcome candidates whose work connects two or more sections.

All qualified candidates are invited to visit the University of Toronto careers website (<https://jobs.utoronto.ca/job/Toronto-Associate-Professor-Professor-Global-Economics-ON/606817817/>) to view the full job posting for further details, application procedures, FAQs, statements and to apply for this opportunity.

We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.

As part of your application, you will be asked to complete a brief Diversity Survey. This survey is voluntary. The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.

If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact [uoft.careers@utoronto.ca](mailto:uoft.careers@utoronto.ca).

**Ad text:**

NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor position for seven years in Microeconomics at the Department of Economics.

We are seeking a highly talented candidate with a key interest in microeconomics. A successful candidate should have a strong publication record and/or highly promising work in the pipeline and should also be an excellent teacher with good skills in communicating insights from microeconomics to students. The successful candidate should preferably be able to teach microeconomic theory at all levels. Outreach to society and dissemination of research are also of importance for the position.

The department has around 50 faculty members and 30 PhD students. It offers an international research environment with a large share of young faculty. The successful candidate will join the [Micro research group](https://www.nhh.no/en/research-projects-and-groups/micro-research-group/) at the department, a strong academic community with an extensive international network. We expect the candidate to be an active member of the Micro group and to contribute to strengthening the group’s activities, which currently span fields such as industrial organization, environmental economics, public economics, and microeconomic theory. Other core fields at the department include behavioural economics, development economics, economic history, labour economics and macroeconomics. The department is particularly committed to providing a stimulating and supportive environment for young faculty and offers a dedicated young faculty development programme. For more information, [visit our webpage](https://www.nhh.no/en/departments/economics/).

To be qualified for the tenure-track position, it should not be more than five years since the PhD degree was achieved (may be extended, for example in connection with statutory leave). For candidates undertaking the PhD, the expected completion of the PhD thesis should be no later than the date of commencement.

The position will involve a competitive teaching load, which also includes some graduate student supervision and administrative duties. Faculty members at NHH are expected to be good teachers. NHH offers the opportunity to participate in a program for university pedagogy, and candidates hired for tenure-track position as Assistant Professor must take one basic module of the program during the fixed-term period. Candidates hired for the tenure-track position as Associate Professor, who cannot document at least 200 hours of pedagogical coursework at the time of promotion to a permanent position, must complete this program within two years.

NHH values effective communication and expects our faculty to have good language skills in both English and Norwegian. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level within three years of appointment to a permanent position. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Associate Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level (The Common European Framework) within three years of appointment to the tenure-track position. NHH offers courses in Norwegian for employees who may not initially have Norwegian or another Scandinavian language proficiency.

The position is based in Bergen, Norway.

**NHH offers:**

* Annual salary of NOK 726 200 – 784 000 (Assistant Professor) or NOK 784 000 – 840 700 (Associate Professor), depending on the level of competence/length of service. The salary may be adjusted during 2027.
* An academically stimulating working environment.
* A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund ([SPK](https://www.spk.no/en/)) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
* Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
* Female associate professors appointed to permanent academic positions may apply for research leave (sabbatical) with half the standard accrual period, in accordance with NHH’s applicable guidelines. This will apply for the first two years of research leave.

Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild and coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for cultural and outdoor activities as well as a family-friendly environment ([explore visitnorway.com](https://www.visitnorway.com/places-to-go/fjord-norway/bergen/)). NHH offers dedicated support to international employees. More information about relocation and onboarding services is available on our [Onboarding Services webpage](https://www.nhh.no/en/about-nhh/nhh-onboarding-services/).

**General information**

The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.

NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, cultural background, age, or disability.

In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates.

The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. In addition, the applicant should provide a teaching statement, which also includes an overview and assessment of the applicants' teaching experience. The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers (for the position of Assistant Professor) or a maximum of 10 published or unpublished research papers (for the position of Associate Professor), a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through this portal.

As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.

Enquiries about the position may be directed to:

* Lars Sørgard, Head of Department, email: [lars.sorgard@nhh.no](mailto:lars.sorgard@nhh.no)
* Morten Sæthre, Professor, email: [morten.saetre@nhh.no](mailto:morten.saetre@nhh.no)
* Mette Soltvedt, Administrative Coordinator, email: [mette.soltvedt@nhh.no](mailto:mette.soltvedt@nhh.no)

**About NHH**

[**NHH Norwegian School of Economics**](https://nhh.no/en/about-nhh/) is one of the leading business schools in Europe. We have an internationally recognised research environment and collaborate with 195 universities and business schools worldwide. NHH is the first choice for students who want to study business administration in Norway. Our activities are characterised by high quality, strong ethical standards, and a collective drive for common goals.

In close partnership with the business community and society, we generate and disseminate new knowledge and create value for a sustainable future. NHH is located in the city of Bergen and has around 3,750 students and 455 employees.

Description

The School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Sustainability Sciences (SoMAS) at Stony Brook University seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor of environmental and resource economics. SoMAS's mission is to advance knowledge and solve critical global and regional problems through the study of human and natural systems. Coastal and marine resources, land use, food systems, and the climate are changing rapidly, and sound management depends on understanding how people, markets, and policies respond to and shape those changes. We seek an economist whose research addresses these questions for living resources (e.g., fisheries, ecosystems and ecosystem services, and food systems), non-living resources (e.g., carbon, energy, water, and ocean and coastal space), or both. Relevant areas include spatially explicit economic analysis of environmental systems, marine spatial planning, land-use transitions, externality pricing, benefit-cost analysis, and the economics of ocean- and land-based climate mitigation. Theoretical, empirical, and quantitative approaches are all welcome. The position offers an economist an unusual opportunity to work alongside oceanographers, atmospheric scientists, ecologists, and sustainability scholars to connect ecosystem dynamics, human behavior, and markets, and to translate that work into effective and socially beneficial policy.

Description of Duties: The successful candidate will establish and sustain an independent, externally funded research program supported by federal agencies (e.g., NSF, NOAA, USDA), state programs, foundations, or nongovernmental organizations. The successful candidate will have a strong commitment to teaching and will teach classes at the undergraduate and graduate levels, as well as mentor students. The candidate will commit to departmental and university service.

Special Notes: This is a tenure-track position. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA.

Campus Description: Stony Brook University, home to many highly ranked graduate research programs, is located 60 miles from New York City on Long Island's scenic North Shore. Our 1,100-acre campus is home to 24,000 undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students and more than 13,500 faculty and staff. SBU is a comprehensive research-intensive university and a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU), which includes 34 public universities among its 62 members. SBU consists of 12 schools and colleges and a teaching hospital that provides state-of-the-art healthcare in the Long Island region. SBU also manages and performs joint research with Brookhaven National Laboratory, the only Department of Energy Laboratory in the Northeast, and shares doctoral programs with Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, a world-renowned molecular biology institute. SBU serves as the anchor of the New York Climate Exchange, located on Governors Island close to Manhattan. Home to the Emerson String Quartet, the Pollock-Krasner House in East Hampton, New York, the Humanities Institute, and the Southampton Arts Program, and with endeavors that extend to the Turkana Basin Institute in Kenya and the Ranomafana National Park in Madagascar, SBU sustains an international reputation that cuts across the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences.

School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Sustainability Sciences: The School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Sustainability Sciences (SoMAS) is the State University of New York's center for marine and atmospheric research, education, and public service. Its three divisions (Atmospheric Sciences, Marine Sciences, and Sustainability Studies) serve approximately 800 graduate and undergraduate students, and its faculty are internationally known for research in atmospheric sciences, all the major disciplines of oceanography (biological, chemical, geological, and physical), and sustainability studies. SoMAS has a strong record of partnership with agencies such as NOAA and the NYS Department of Environmental Conservation and with regional programs such as the Peconic Estuary Partnership. It also provides scientific leadership for the New York Climate Exchange on Governors Island, which aims to be a leading hub for climate finance, policy guidance, and innovation in scaling investment in climate action. Excellent opportunities for collaboration exist within SoMAS and across Stony Brook, including with the Department of Economics, the Institute for Advanced Computational Science, and Brookhaven National Laboratory. For more information, please visit <http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu> and our strategic plan at <https://www.stonybrook.edu/somas/about/strategic-plan.html>.

Interest in or experience with interdisciplinary collaboration, including with natural scientists. Experience or demonstrated potential in teaching and mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate students

To apply, visit <https://apptrkr.com/9909345>.

Application Instructions: Complete applications should include a single page cover letter, curriculum vitae, a job market paper or other representative research paper, three letters of reference at the time of submission, and separate statements of: i) current and proposed research; ii) teaching and mentoring philosophy, interests, and previous experiences (e.g., courses taught, activities); iii) experience ensuring a fair, supportive work environment where all colleagues have the opportunity to contribute and succeed. The Department of Economics invites applicants within the following fields:

* Macroeconomics
* Household Finance
* Family and Demographic Economics

**Requirements**

Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Economics by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, and no later than September 30, 2027. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027. The position is for four years, with 25% of the working time devoted to teaching.

Candidates must provide evidence of excellence in research of the highest international caliber in one of the fields listed above. This can be demonstrated by an innovative job market paper with a significant contribution to the literature, high-quality working papers, (forthcoming) publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals, strong recommendations by referees who themselves have a record of excellence in research of the highest international caliber, the submitted research statement, presentations at significant conferences, and awards and accolades.

We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths. To be considered for a position, candidates should motivate their application in light of the Department’s overall research profile and location.

**About the project**

The postdoctoral position is financed by the research project [HOWFER](https://www.sv.uio.no/econ/english/research/projects/howfer/index.html) (Housing, Wealth, and Fertility in High-income Societies), led by Associate Professor Martin Blomhoff Holm. The project combines macroeconomics, household finance, and family economics to analyze how rising house prices and wealth concentration have contributed to falling fertility in high-income countries. Using Norwegian administrative data linking wealth, housing, and family formation for the entire population, the work will estimate the causal effect of house prices on fertility, develop a search-and-matching framework to explain the rise in childlessness and singlehood, and build structural models to evaluate which policies most effectively affect fertility. The postdoctoral researcher will contribute both to the empirical and theoretical parts of the project, in collaboration with the core research team.

Candidates should articulate how they can contribute to and strengthen the project.

**We offer**

The Department of Economics at the University of Oslo offers:

* A stimulating and international research environment with multiple research groups and seminar series.
* A friendly and inclusive workplace that allows for a good work-life balance.
* Access to Norway’s excellent public services and welfare schemes, including generous parental leave provisions and accessible (and affordable) childcare (including the university’s kindergartens).
* Norway’s capital, with its rich cultural life and easy access to nature.

**How to apply**

The application deadline is November 30, 2026. Applications must be submitted online at <https://econjobmarket.org/>.

A complete application must include a cover letter, a current curriculum vitae, a research statement outlining current and future research interests and how the candidate’s research profile matches one or more of the fields listed in the posting, a job market paper (clearly labeled), other working papers or publications, and three recent letters of reference (on letterhead, dated, and signed) uploaded directly by referees.

Interviews will be conducted online around the European Job Market, 14-17 December. We will invite a limited number of candidates for job talks/campus visits in January or early February.

**About the department**

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest-ranked educational and research institution, with 28 000 students and 7000 employees. The Department of Economics is among the top-ranked departments for economic research in Norway. The Department offers Bachelor's and Masters' programmes, as well as a doctoral program with approximately 20 students. The department has attracted a number of ERC grants, it hosts a research center in public economics, Norwegian Fiscal Studies (NFS), and in international economics, the Norwegian Centre for International Economics (NORCIE).

The University of Oslo has a personnel policy objective of achieving a balanced gender composition; see [Gender equality initiatives at UiO](https://www.uio.no/english/for-employees/competence/gender-equality/index.html). We welcome employees with diverse expertise, life experience and perspectives.

For questions about this position, please contact project leader Martin Blomhoff Holm, email: [m.b.holm@econ.uio.no](mailto:m.b.holm@econ.uio.no) or the Head of Administration, Brita Langeid, email: [brita.langeid@econ.uio.no](mailto:brita.langeid@econ.uio.no).

We are the leading partner in the [Finnish Centre of Excellence in Tax Systems Research (FIT),](http://www.taxresearch.fi/) FIT conducts research on the effects and design of multiple aspects of public policy. We seek an accomplished early-career academic with the potential to organize and conduct innovative, top-quality research in their field. The candidate's research can focus on any field of economics. **Ad text:**

Hushcrasher does applied research for the video game industry. We measure the video game market, predict its outcomes, and optimize its key decisions. Our ambition is to solve its hardest problems: revenue forecasting, optimal pricing, causal factors of success. We turn business questions into optimization problems, helping studios, publishers, and investors make better decisions.

We are looking for our first hire. The role involves taking the lead on machine learning and data science, and building the scientific core of the company with us. You design the models at the heart of our products (forecasting, demand estimation, game similarity through embeddings), help decide which ones we build next, and take them all the way to production. Part of your time goes to research you initiate yourself, with the goal of gaining a better understanding of the video game market. We work as peers: you own your projects.

Questions you might work on:

* What makes two games similar, and how can we better leverage images and other non-textual data to do so?
* What are the best early signals to predict a game’s success, and how precise could we be?
* At what price should a game launch to maximize its revenue, and how should that price vary across time and markets?
* When should a game be released, and how much does the competition matter?
* How much does it cost to make a game? How likely is it to overrun its initial budget?
* Which small design tweaks would causally raise a game’s odds of success?
* How can we detect emerging trends, and declining ones?

Hushcrasher started from the urge to take a subject as far as it can go. We are looking for people who have done the same, whatever the topic: research you led, a model you took to production, a company you founded, a tool people actually use.

Your strength is machine learning and applied mathematics, to complement our CTO, an economist and data scientist. You are versatile, as comfortable with theory as with shipping, and at ease in a young company. You treat your work as a craft and hold a high bar.

Hushcrasher was founded in January 2026 by a PhD economist, and a former VC advisor turned game studio manager. Since then, the company secured €800k in grants, put our first models into production, launched a newsletter read by 1,300 industry professionals, and started building a demand model with an economist at ZEW and advice from a PhD candidate at Harvard. We work fully remote within the EU, with a few in-person meetups in Paris during the year. We offer equity and sponsor French work permits for candidates based outside the EU.

If that sounds like you, we should talk.

[**The Department of Economics**](https://www.wu.ac.at/en/economics "Department of Economics_WU_Vienna University of Economics and Business") of the WU Vienna University of Economics and Business invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position (post-doc) in **International Economics**. The position is a 100% (40 hours/week, employee subject to the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement for University Staff - Angestellte/r gemäß Kollektivvertrag für die Arbeitnehmer/innen der Universitäten) and is expected to begin on September 1, 2027. The gross monthly salary, paid 14 times per year, is €5.980,80 subject to adjustment if candidates can document relevant prior professional experience.

The Department of Economics offers an active and internationally oriented research environment. The successful candidate’s research focus should be in the field of International Economics. You will join the faculty of the Department of Economics and are expected to provide a good fit to its current research environment, as well as cultivate excellence and contribute to the department's research, teaching, and service activities in the department.

**Your Profile:** Applicants should have

* a solid academic qualification (PhD or equivalent) in economics (or a related field),
* high-quality research output (job market paper(s) and/or publications in international peer-reviewed journals) related to the field of international economics,
* academic mobility, proven by either having completed their PhD or doctoral degree at a university other than WU, or having completed an uninterrupted postdoc employment period (in a tenure-track or non-tenure-track position) of at least two years and with an extent of employment of at least 20 hours per week at another university or non-academic research institution,
* a commitment to excellence in teaching, including the willingness to use multimedia teaching methods,
* experience in the acquisition of third-party funded projects is of advantage, and
* ability to enlarge and deepen the network of contacts to the international academic community.

Knowledge of German is not required, but an asset.

**Application Procedure:**

1. **Stage One**  
   Applicants must complete a WU application form, which can be accessed by clicking on the University’s [online recruitment system](https://jobs.wu.ac.at/Assistant-Professor-tenure-track-qualification-agreement-eng-j2954.html) (ID 2954) by November 25 (midnight CET). Please do not include research papers or references with this application.
2. **Stage Two (to be completed in conjunction with stage one – it is important that both stages are completed in full)** You must apply online at <https://econjobmarket.org/> by November 25 (midnight UTC) in order to be considered for the first round of interviews at the [European Job Market, EEA Job Market Meeting, Online, 14-17 December 2026](https://www.europeanjobmarketofeconomists.org/). Please submit a cover letter, a CV, up to two research papers, three letters of reference, and teaching evaluations.

If you are interested in a job with diverse responsibilities in a pleasant, stimulating work environment, please submit your application by November 25, 2026.

**We are looking forward to hearing from you!**

The ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research in Mannheim, Germany, is one of the leading economic research institutes in Europe. It is integrated into an extensive national and international network of universities and research institutes. The ZEW is looking to fill the following position in the Research Unit "Pensions and Sustainable Financial Markets"

We are looking for an applied economist with a strong research profile in empirical research on household finance and pensions. The successful candidate will contribute to the unit’s research agenda on the challenges that demographic change, digitalisation, and climate change pose to pensions and financial markets, with a particular focus on household finance.

Your Profile  
• A completed PhD (or near completion) in economics or finance  
• Excellent skills in quantitative methods, such as quasi-experimental methods for administrative data, survey design, and survey and field experiments  
• Fluency in English, German is helpful but not required

• Conducting high-quality empirical research in household finance, pension economics, and related fields targeting publications in leading economic and finance journals  
• Communicating scientific findings to the public, stakeholders, and policymakers  
• Conceptualizing and managing third-party funded research projects

• A full-time position for two years, with the option to extend for up to three additional years and a possible further one-year extension  
• Salary and benefits in line with the German public sector pay scale  
• A position without any teaching responsibilities  
• Support for postdoctoral qualification and international research visits  
• A dynamic, collaborative, and policy-relevant research environment

IF INTERESTED, please submit your application including a cover letter, CV, two letters of reference, and one writing sample (e.g., published paper, working paper, thesis chapter, or PhD thesis) by November 25, 2026, via the online application form on our website. **Ad text:**

The Public Economics Department analyzes how financial, fiscal, and social policies influence economic decisions made by individuals, households, and companies. The department’s key focus is on fiscal and social policy in Germany, with analyses based on microsimulation models and microeconometric methods. Of particular interest are the behavioral patterns of households, companies, and policy makers, as well as the distributional effects of fiscal and social policy. These are assessed not only at national level, but also at local, regional, and EU levels.

**Starting preferably on 1st September 2027,** DIW Berlin is looking for a

Postdoc (f/m/x)
---------------

**(full-time, part-time is possible)**

This position is suitable for furthering scientific training according to Section 2, paragraph 1 of the Act on Fixed-Term Employment Contracts in Academic (WissZeitVG).

Your responsibilities:

- You will conduct and manage high-quality scientific research with the aim of publishing in leading journals in Economics

- You will contribute to the department's research agenda, including work on demographic change, the distributional effects of tax and transfer systems and household behavior over the lifecycle

- You will carry out scientific research within the framework of third-party funded projects

- You will develop your own research ideas and prepare applications for third-party funding

- Teaching activities are optional

Your qualifications:

- A completed master’s degree in economics or a closely related field

- PhD in Economics or a related field, with a strong interest in Applied Economics and a particular focus on Public Economics, Social Policy, Labor Economics, and Distributional Economics, including policy evaluation

- Specialized knowledge of empirical tools, especially (micro-)econometric methods and structural models, and experience working with micro-level and aggregated data

- Demonstrated potential to contribute substantially to academic research and policy analysis, including the ability to recognize and articulate differing viewpoints and an open attitude toward interdisciplinary cooperation

- Willingness to work in an international environment and collaborate across disciplines

- Record of published and/or forthcoming articles in relevant journals

- Excellent command of English

What we offer:

A modern, well-equipped workplace at a research institute with around 300 colleagues, where diversity, equal opportunities and a healthy work-life balance are guiding principles applied across all areas of work. Working time arrangements tailored to individual needs, flexible working hours and remote working are integral parts of our working culture.

DIW Berlin supports your professional and personal qualification and advancement via internal and external career development opportunities and annual performance reviews.

You are paid according to the collective agreement for the public sector (Tarifvertrag des öffentlichen Dienstes,TVöD Bund), which includes an annual bonus as well as a company pension with VBL Ost.

Through our partnership with a leading sports network, you can enjoy discounted access to a diverse range of partner gyms and sports activities.

Your workplace is centrally located in the heart of Berlin, which is convenient to public transportation. As a DIW Berlin employee, you are eligible for a discounted VBB company ticket or Deutschlandticket Job, which is partially subsidized.

The position is limited to 3 years, with the option of extending for an additional 3 years. Remuneration is paid according to TVöD Bund, salary group EG14.

Application and information:

We value diversity and welcome all applications regardless of gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic or social origin. If you’re interested in the position, we are excited to hear from you!

Please apply exclusively online through our application portal by 23 November 2026, stating the reference number STT-1-26 and including a cover/motivation letter, CV, copy of your job market paper and your degree and work certificates and references. Please do not include a photo.

You can access the application portal via our career page at

<https://www.diw.de/de/diw_01.c.617346.de/karriere.html>

Please note that only applications submitted through the portal can be considered. If you have any questions about the online application, feel free to contact recruiting@diw.de.

For information about the job responsibilities, please contact Prof. Dr. Peter Haan (phaan@diw.de).

You can find more information about DIW Berlin on our homepage at www.diw.de.

First round interviews will be conducted online in coordination with the European Job Market for Economists in December 2026.

Founded in 1925, DIW Berlin (the German Institute for Economic Research) is one of the leading economic research institutes in Germany. The Institute analyzes the economic and social aspects of topical issues, formulating and disseminating policy advice based on its research findings. DIW Berlin is part of both the national and international scientific communities, provides research infrastructure to academics all over the world, and promotes the next generation of scientists. A member of the Leibniz Association, DIW Berlin is independent and primarily publicly funded.

**Ad text:**

Hanken School of Economics invites applications for an Assistant Professor (tenure-track) in Finance

beginning no later than August 2027, or as otherwise agreed. The position is at the Finance Unit at the Department of Finance and Economics in Helsinki. For this position, we will consider candidates in all fields of Finance.

The position is part of the Hanken tenure track system. It is open to talented individuals who have potential for an excellent scientific career. Individuals placed on the Hanken tenure track have the possibility to advance in their career through regular performance assessments, which consider their merits in all relevant qualification areas in accordance with [Hanken’s tenure track guidelines](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/hankens-tenure-track-system).

Hanken School of Economics is a research-oriented business school offering education in English and Swedish. Hanken’s Finance unit is committed to high-quality teaching and research. We offer full scale graduate and undergraduate programs.

We have a strong research climate, reflected in a growing volume and range of research activities. We value high-quality, practice-oriented research, as evidenced by our publications in top-ranked journals. In addition, Hanken's Finance unit is an active partner in the Graduate School of Finance (GSF), which offers the national doctoral program in finance. GSF also organizes seminars and workshops for faculty members and doctoral students.

Requirements  
The applicants will be reviewed based on their research, teaching, institutional service, and societal impact. Applicants should hold a doctoral degree (or be near completion of the doctorate) in Finance (or a related field). When evaluating the applicants’ qualifications, the main focus will be on the potential to conduct high-quality scientific research and the potential to provide high-quality teaching. A focus on asset pricing is considered a strong merit.

Being a stand-alone business school with strong Nordic roots, Hanken offers degree programmes in Swedish and English. For this position, applicants are required to have fluent command of English, knowledge of Swedish is considered a merit. Hanken supports its faculty in learning the Swedish language, which serves as the administrative language of the business school.

Academic staff at Hanken are expected to carry out and supervise scientific research, provide academic teaching, closely follow the advances of their field, and contribute service to Hanken, the academic community, and society. Teaching tasks are allocated based on the curriculum needs of the subject and by considering relevant expertise.

The full-time position has an annual working time of 1612 hours. During the academic year, it is expected that a minimum average of three days per week is spent at the office in Helsinki to actively contribute to the research and teaching environment. Hanken requires academic employees to reside and work in Finland, and it offers relocation support for applicants coming from outside Finland.

Salary  
The salary is based on the university salary system in Finland (includes employee healthcare as well as pension and holiday contributions). The exact salary level depends on the recruited individual’s qualifications. Hanken will support the selected employee with a start-up research budget, and additional research, travel and teaching development grants can also be applied for. Hanken rewards excellence in both research and teaching.

For more Information  
For additional information, please contact Head of Department Jesper Haga ([jesper.haga@hanken.fi)](mailto:jesper.haga@hanken.fi)) or Head of Subject Karl Felixson ([karl.felixson@hanken.fi)](mailto:karl.felixson@hanken.fi)).

General instructions for applicants are provided [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/hankens-tenure-track-system/research-track-0). Also, read more about Hanken as an employer [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/node/2413861).

Recruitment process and timeline  
The application deadline is 22 November 2026. Selected candidates will be interviewed online shortly after the application deadline. Short-listed candidates will be invited to on-site campus visits including an interview and research presentation.

How to apply  
The application is to be addressed to the Rector and application materials should include:

* CV (proposed content [here](https://tenk.fi/en/advice-and-materials/template-researchers-curriculum-vitae)), including list of publications.
* Personal statement, which includes a description of past research and its scientific quality, academic impact, plans for future research and a description of the candidate’s service to the department and university and a description of the candidate’s societal impact.
* Teaching portfolio (proposed content [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/applications-and-selection-process)).
* Copies of no more than five research publications, including a ‘job market’ paper
* Three letters of reference from academic researchers, to be submitted via [Econjobmarket](https://econjobmarket.org/positions?show=all&type=reg&searchType=quick&saved_search_id=0&cutoffDate=2007-01-01&position_type_id=&category_id=&iso2=&oid=1337#ad-11885) or directly to Hanken via [humanresources@hanken.fi](mailto:humanresources@hanken.fi).

Please submit all application materials in English in Hanken’s recruitment database LAURA, <https://hanken.rekrytointi.com/paikat/?o=A_A&jid=405>. The application deadline is 22 November 2026.

*Hanken School of Economics is one of the leading business schools in the Nordic countries. It is located in Finland, with campuses in Helsinki and Vaasa. Hanken offers a range of B.Sc., M.Sc., EMBA, PhD, and Executive Development programmes taught mainly in English and Swedish. Hanken has 2 725 Bachelor and Master’s students, and 118 Doctoral students. The School has close ties to the business community and an active alumni network with over 13 800 alumni working in more than 70 countries. The School is accredited by AACSB, AMBA, and EQUIS. The Master’s programme was ranked 56 in the Masters in Management by Financial Times in 2026. Hanken is also recognized for its research quality, its international orientation, and its focus on sustainability.*
