Národná banka Slovenska (NBS), the central bank of the Slovak Republic, invites applications for a Senior Economist position to lead applied, policy-relevant research at the intersection of climate change and central banking.

NBS is a member of the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). It contributes to the formulation and implementation of euro area monetary policy, supervises Slovakia’s financial market, and works to safeguard financial stability. Working within the ESCB network, you will contribute to European policy discussion on climate change while shaping NBS’s climate agenda. You will have access to unique and highly granular central-bank datasets, collaborate with a broad network of ESCB climate researchers, and bridge quantitative analysis with real monetary and financial stability policy decisions.

While climate economics is a central focus of this vacancy, NBS is also interested in outstanding economists with a broader profile in applied macroeconomics and monetary economics. We therefore encourage applications from candidates whose research can contribute more broadly to NBS’s analysis of the Slovak and euro area economies and to monetary-policy discussions within the Eurosystem. Relevant fields may include inflation, labour markets, productivity, fiscal policy, international trade and competitiveness, business cycles, and monetary-policy transmission.

**The role**

You will lead independent research and analytical projects on climate change and its implications for one or more of the following core domains: monetary policy, financial stability, energy markets, and central-bank investment portfolios. Your analysis will directly support institutional reporting, strategic decision-making, and delivery of the NBS’s Climate Strategy. This role emphasises rigorous, evidence-based policy insights over purely academic research.

Reporting to the Head of Unit, you will work closely with colleagues across economic research, monetary policy analysis, and other departments.

**Your key responsibilities will include:**

* Identifying high-relevance policy research questions informed by priorities set by NBS management, the Climate Committee’s agenda, and wider EU and ESCB policy and research developments.
* Designing and executing rigorous quantitative analytical projects using appropriate economic frameworks, granular datasets, and state-of-the-art quantitative methods.
* Translating complex academic findings into actionable policy insights and clearly communicating both the implications and limitations of findings for subject-matter specialists and senior decisionmakers.
* Producing policy briefs, working papers, public-facing blog posts, and internal analytical notes.
* Mentoring junior economists and engaging with the broader European central banking and climate research community.

Your work will be rooted in NBS’s institutional priorities, with opportunities for academic publication and related research, subject to available capacity.

**Qualifications**

Required:

* PhD in Economics, Finance, or a closely related quantitative field awarded prior to the contract start date.
* Advanced experience in applied econometrics, data analytics, and programming with practical familiarity with software such as Stata, R, Python, QGIS, or MATLAB.
* Excellent command of English; **Knowledge of** **Slovak is NOT required**.

Assets:

* A track record of research on climate-related macroeconomics, financial stability risks, energy economics, or sustainable finance.
* A demonstrated research expertise in applied macroeconomics, monetary economics, or a related policy-relevant field may substitute for a specific research background in climate economics.
* Experience writing policy-oriented research for audiences in central banks or other public-sector institutions.
* Experience presenting research findings and policy analysis to mixed audiences of economists, policymakers, and technical experts.
* Strong collaboration and communication skills, including the ability to convey complex analytical insights to non-specialist audiences.
* A proactive and innovative approach to problem-solving.

**Employment terms and compensation**

This is intended as a long-term position. In line with NBS's standard employment practice, new hires are initially appointed on a one-year contract with a three-month probationary period. Subject to satisfactory performance, the appointment is expected to continue and may lead to a permanent position.

Senior economists typically earn €50,000 or more gross annually, including variable pay. The statutory minimum basic pay for this position is €2,400 gross per month.

We offer:

* An international, collaborative working environment with direct access to senior economists, researchers, and policymakers across the European Central Bank network and Network for Greening the Financial System.
* Opportunity to contribute to policy decisions with wider institutional and societal implications.
* Early involvement in impactful analytical work, with opportunities to grow your research, presentation, and policy communication skills.
* Access to NBS-funded training, seminars, and conference participation.
* Flexible working hours and fully funded annual team-building retreats.
* Attractive benefits and an office located in a modern European capital, easily reachable by international commuters and close to major transport links (e.g., Vienna International Airport).

**Application and selection**

Please submit a CV, a one-page cover letter explaining your interest in the position and your suitability for it, a sample of recent research or an alternative relevant analytical work, and at least two letters of recommendation by 22 November 2026, 23:59 UTC. These materials will form an important part of the evaluation process.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an online interview, starting in December 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Selection follows standard economics-recruitment practices. We are looking for an economist with a strong focus on applied policy research. Our evaluation will focus on your broader analytical capabilities rather than solely on the topic of your academic job-market paper. You are welcome to submit an alternative work sample if it demonstrates a stronger fit with this role.

There are **NO** **nationality restrictions**. Successful candidates must obtain any necessary visas and residence or work permits. NBS assists with permits but not visas.

**Ad text:**

Hanken School of Economics invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor (tenure track) in Economics, with the appointment beginning no later than September 2027 (negotiable). The position is based in the Economics Unit in Helsinki.

The position
------------

Candidates from all fields of economics will be considered for the position of Assistant or Associate Professor. Some preference will be given to candidates working in political economics, broadly defined. Teaching in Swedish is expected.

The position is part of Hanken’s research-oriented tenure-track system and is open to individuals with the potential for an excellent scientific career. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to advance through evaluations that consider merits in all relevant areas in accordance with [Hanken’s tenure track guidelines](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/hankens-tenure-track-system). The Assistant Professor position is fixed-term for 5 years, with the possibility to apply for a 2-year extension. Promotion to Associate Professor is subject to a tenure evaluation in accordance with Hanken’s tenure track guidelines. The Associate Professor position is permanent.

Economics at Hanken
-------------------

Hanken School of Economics is a research-oriented business school offering education in English and Swedish. Hanken’s Economics Unit is committed to high-quality teaching and research, with strengths in industrial organisation, behavioural and experimental economics, labour economics and empirical and theoretical microeconomics more broadly. We offer comprehensive undergraduate, master’s and doctoral programmes.

Helsinki Graduate School of Economics
-------------------------------------

Hanken’s Economics Unit is an active partner in the Helsinki Graduate School of Economics (Helsinki GSE). Helsinki GSE brings together economics faculty from three Finnish universities: Aalto University, Hanken School of Economics and the University of Helsinki. Its mission is to produce outstanding research with maximum academic and societal impact, educate the next generation of world-class economists, and offer excellent training across disciplinary boundaries. Helsinki GSE collaborates closely with the VATT Institute for Economic Research (<https://www.vatt.fi/en/>). Helsinki GSE offers a versatile and active research environment and hosts eleven research groups in various fields of economics. Teaching within Helsinki GSE is coordinated among its partner universities to maximise its impact on students and society. Hanken and Helsinki GSE are conveniently located in central Helsinki.

For more information, please visit the [Economics unit](https://www.hanken.fi/en/departments-centres/department-finance-and-economics/economics) and [Helsinki GSE](https://www.helsinkigse.fi/).

Requirements
------------

Applicants will be evaluated based on their research, teaching, institutional service and societal impact. Applicants on the assistant professor level should hold a doctoral degree, or be close to completing one, in economics or a related field. Particular emphasis will be placed on applicants’ potential to conduct high-quality scientific research and provide high-quality teaching in economics.

In addition to the requirements for an assistant professor, applicants for the associate professor level are expected to have demonstrated internationally high levels of research within the scientific field of the position, high levels in teaching and contributed through institutional service and societal impact.

As an independent business school with strong Nordic roots, Hanken offers high-quality degree programmes in Swedish and English. Applicants for the current position are required to have a fluent command of both English and Swedish. Teaching in Swedish is expected as part of the position's responsibilities.

Academic staff at Hanken are expected to conduct and supervise scientific research, provide high-quality academic teaching, remain abreast of developments in their field, and contribute to Hanken, the academic community and society. Teaching duties are allocated based on the curriculum needs of the subject and the appointee’s relevant expertise.

The full-time position has an annual working time of 1,612 hours. During the academic year, the appointee is expected to work at the office in Helsinki for an average of at least three days per week to actively contribute to the research and teaching environment. Hanken requires academic employees to reside and work in Finland and provides relocation support for applicants moving to Finland from abroad.

Salary
------

The salary is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities and includes occupational health care as well as pension and holiday benefits. The exact salary level depends on the appointee’s qualifications. Hanken provides the selected candidate with a start-up research budget. Additional grants for research, travel and teaching development may also be applied for. Hanken rewards excellence in both research and teaching.

Further information
-------------------

For further information, please contact Professor Topi Miettinen, [topi.miettinen@hanken.fi](mailto:topi.miettinen@hanken.fi).

General instructions for applicants are available [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/hankens-tenure-track-system). More information about Hanken as an employer is available [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/node/2413861).

Recruitment process and timeline
--------------------------------

The application deadline is 17 November 2026. Candidates will be interviewed online after the application deadline in the European Job Market Online Interview Window, December 14-17, 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an on-campus visit that includes an interview and a research presentation.

How to apply
------------

The application should be addressed to the Rector and must include:

* Cover letter in which the applicant specifies the position for which they are applying (associate professor or assistant professor)
* A curriculum vitae, including a list of publications. A standard economics Job Market CV is sufficient. One commonly used CV format is available at [here](https://tenk.fi/en/advice-and-materials/template-researchers-curriculum-vitae).
* Personal statement describing the applicant’s previous research and its scientific quality and academic impact, plans for future research, service to the department and university, and societal impact. For candidates applying for the associate professor level, the personal statement should also include a description of research collaboration with other scholars, contributions to international scientific networks, involvement in applications for external research funding, and contributions to the pedagogical development in the department or university beyond own teaching. The personal statement needs to be written with the announced position in mind.
* Copies of five research publications that best demonstrate high scientific quality research
* A teaching portfolio (proposed content [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/applications-and-selection-process))
* Three letters of reference from academic researchers, submitted through [EconJobMarket](https://econjobmarket.org/positions?show=all&type=reg&searchType=quick&saved_search_id=0&cutoffDate=2007-01-01&position_type_id=&category_id=&iso2=&oid=1337#ad-11885) or sent directly to Hanken at [humanresources@hanken.fi](mailto:humanresources@hanken.fi). If you apply for an associate professor position only, letters are not required but recommended.

Please submit all application materials in English through Hanken’s recruitment database LAURA, <https://hanken.rekrytointi.com/paikat/?o=A_A&jid=407>. The application deadline is 17 November 2026.

About Hanken
------------

*Hanken School of Economics is one of the leading business schools in the Nordic countries. It is located in Finland, with campuses in Helsinki and Vaasa. Hanken offers a range of B.Sc., M.Sc., EMBA, PhD, and Executive Development programmes taught mainly in English and Swedish. Hanken has 2 725 Bachelor and Master’s students, and 118 Doctoral researchers. The School has close ties to the business community and an active alumni network with over 13 800 alumni working in more than 70 countries. The School is accredited by AACSB, AMBA, and EQUIS. The Master’s programme was ranked 56 in the Masters in Management by Financial Times in 2026. Hanken is also recognized for its research quality, its international orientation, and its focus on sustainability.*

The Department of Wealth Creation at the Lake Lucerne Institute (LLUI Wealth) aims to fill vacancies for Postdoctoral Fellow positions. The appointments are for a term of three years and can be renewed once for a total contract length of six years.

**Background**

LLUI Wealth is committed to advancing high-impact research that meets the rigorous standards of top-tier academic journals in economics and finance. Additionally, it maintains strong connections with the asset management industry, ensuring its research is practical and highly relevant to the financial sector.

As a Postdoctoral Fellow, you will join LLUI’s Department of Wealth Creation, work with its team, and be supervised by four affiliated faculty members: Michael Weber, Francesco D’Acunto, Andreas Neuhierl, and Alberto Rossi. They are leading researchers specializing in asset pricing, investments, and behavioral finance. They lead the department’s main focus areas, which cover cutting-edge areas in finance such as big data analytics, machine learning, and behavioral and cognitive finance.

Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to supervise predocs and (once the positions are created) PhD students, collaborate with LLUI-affiliated faculty and researchers on high-impact academic research projects, and disseminate research with national and international presentations as well as academic publications.

**Your Role**

* Active participation in the strategic development of the research program
* National and international networking
* Engaging in independent research in the areas of asset management, asset pricing, behavioral finance, or household finance at the level of top journals in Economics and Finance
* Supervising, mentoring, and coordinating pre-doctoral research assistants
* Presenting results at national and international conferences
* Assisting with grant applications

* PhD in Economics, Finance, Behavioral Sciences, or related fields (obtained before July 1, 2027)
* Strong quantitative background and analytical skills
* Proficiency in conducting statistical analyses

LLUI Wealth provides a vibrant research environment with ample resources to further develop an existing research program. These include pre-doctoral fellows who can assist in data collection and analysis, internal grants for data acquisition, and a research budget for presenting at conferences. LLUI Wealth regularly hosts leading international academics at its conferences, workshops, PhD summer school, and internal seminar series.

**We are committed to equality**

LLUI is committed to equality in general and gender equality in particular. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of origin, gender, age, or background. Our commitments are set out in our Gender Equality Plan.

**Application**

The positions are available from July 1, 2027, though other dates may be considered. Salary and benefits are competitive. Please contact Felix von Meyerinck (felix.vonmeyerinck@llui.org) with any questions you may have. Please send your complete application (CV, cover letter, and job market paper) to jobs.wealth.postdoc@llui.org and ask three references to send their letters to the same address. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Incomplete applications or applications that do not match the published profile will not be considered.

Applications are invited for a post-doctoral Research Fellow in the Department of Economics at University College London to work on the research project “Liquidity Policies in the 21st Century” which has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) (Consolidator Award) under the European Union’s Horizon (2021-2027) research and innovation programme.

Professor Saleem Bahaj, the Principal Investigator, is seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to work on this exciting project from September 2027 for two years (negotiable).

About the Research Project

Central banks are the guardians of financial stability, but modern markets face unprecedented risks that traditional policies struggle to address. The ERC-funded “Liquidity Policies in the 21st Century” project is redesigning liquidity strategies to fit this complex landscape. By examining how banks manage reserves and deposits under today’s regulatory constraints, the project identifies more efficient ways to control inflation and fiscal costs. It further investigates how lender-of-last-resort support can be tailored to distinguish between cautious hedgers and risky speculators. Finally, the project explores how targeting specific institutions can maximise the economic boost of liquidity injections. These insights provide a vital roadmap for policymakers to ensure Europe’s financial systems remain resilient and effective in a rapidly evolving global economy.

What We Offer

Professor Saleem Bahaj, the Principal Investigator, is seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to work on the “Liquidity Policies in the 21st Century” project. The researcher will be appointed from September 2027 for two years (negotiable). The Appointment will be on UCL salary scale Grade 7, £47,186 to £55,099 per annum inclusive of London Allowance, dependent upon experience and qualifications.

The UCL full-time working week totals 36.5 hours. Annual leave is 27 days per year. In addition, staff benefit from six College closure days per year. The person appointed will work at the offices of the Department of Economics, Drayton House, 30 Gordon Street, London WC1H 0AX.

The Department of Finance at the Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University Rotterdam is looking for enthusiastic, forward-thinking and research-driven candidates who can grow into excellent and impactful researchers and committed teachers in our undergraduate, master, and executive education programmes.

### Introduction

Are you ready for a role that will help to create the future of finance? You’ll join a dynamic and international department of dedicated educators and ambitious academics in a department that engages in top quality research and hosts specialised conferences and seminars. Research and education focus on positive change that enables people and organisations to thrive; RSM’s finance programmes and courses for bachelor, master and executive students address topics at the cutting edge of the field of finance, including sustainable finance and climate risk, corporate finance, asset management, credit risk, financial innovation, FinTech, entrepreneurial finance and corporate governance.

In RSM’s Department of Finance we conduct world-class research in all areas of finance. We are responsible for a very successful MSc programme in Finance and Investments, ranked by the *Financial Times*. The department also contributes to the school’s undergraduate, MBA and PhD programmes and to the MSc in Business Analytics & Management. Our faculty regularly publishes in the top journals in the field, such as *Journal of Finance, Review of Financial Studies, Journal of Financial Economics, Review of Finance, Management Science* and *Journal of Monetary Economics*. We cooperate with the Erasmus School of Economics via the Erasmus Research Institute of Management ([ERIM](https://www.erim.eur.nl/)) by having, e.g., joint seminar series. We regularly host [impactful events](https://www.rsm.nl/faculty-research/departments/finance/conferences/), such as the Conferences on Professional Asset Management and the Liquidity Conferences.

You are invited to apply for one of our newest faculty positions at [Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University (RSM)](https://www.rsm.nl/) as tenure track assistant professor in the Department of Finance, starting on September 1, 2027.

### Job description

In our department, you will:

* Conduct research of high quality to be submitted to top journals in the field (*Journal of Finance, Journal of Financial Economics, Review of Financial Studies, JFQA* and *Review of Finance*), management (*Management Science*) or economics.
* Participate in workshops, seminars, and conferences, supported by a personal research budget.
* Build an international network and gain visibility in the field.
* Develop your teaching skills by obtaining a University Teaching Qualification (UTQ) during the first three years of the tenure track.
* Engage in teaching innovation, and teach courses in our bachelor and master programmes.
* Teach in executive education (MBA, Executive MBA, open and custom programmes) in the second half of the tenure track (when applicable).
* Contribute to a collegial atmosphere in the department and take new initiatives.
* Engage with RSM’s mission to be a force for positive change in the world.

### Job requirements

We’re interested in you if you:

* Possess a PhD in Finance, or if you’re in the final year of your PhD study.
* Can demonstrate the potential for outstanding achievements in research and teaching.
* Have a good command of the English language.
* A strong commitment to high-quality research as well as evidence of ability to conduct impactful work and to publish in top finance journals.
* The ability to contribute to the department’s teaching activities at bachelor, master and MBA level.

We’re looking for you if you are:

* An inspired, ambitious, and competent researcher, with a strong commitment to high-quality research
* Enthusiastic about teaching, and an able presenter
* Familiar with online education platforms and with techniques for inspiring successful blended learning
* Possess strong English language skills at C1 level, in both writing and speaking
* Have well-developed analytical, communication and social competences.

### Employment conditions and benefits

Erasmus University Rotterdam aspires to be an equitable and inclusive community. We nurture an open culture, where everyone is supported to fulfil their full potential. We see inclusivity of talent as the basis of our successes, and the diversity of perspectives and people as a highly valued outcome. EUR provides equal opportunities to all employees and applicants regardless of gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, age, neurodiversity, functional impairment, citizenship, or any other aspect which makes them unique. We look forward to welcoming you to our community.

### Employer

Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University ([RSM](http://www.rsm.nl/)) is one of Europe’s top-ranked business schools. RSM provides ground-breaking research and education furthering excellence in all aspects of management and is based in the international port city of Rotterdam – a vital nexus of business, logistics and trade. RSM’s primary focus is on developing business leaders with international careers who can become a force for positive change by carrying their innovative mindset into a sustainable future. Our first-class range of bachelor, master, MBA, PhD and executive programmes encourage them to become critical, creative, caring and collaborative thinkers and doers.

RSM is an equal opportunity employer and explicitly encourages applications from candidates of all genders, ethnicities, and nationalities.

### Department

The Department of Finance at RSM has a large international faculty educated at renowned institutions in Europe, the USA, and Asia. The department has a strong research tradition evidenced by publications in top journals, an active PhD programme, and research visits to leading schools in the world.

The department is part of the Erasmus Finance Group, which includes the Erasmus School of Economics. Erasmus Finance runs a regular seminar series with speakers from top international schools, brown bag seminars, several annual conferences, and a visitor programme with eminent finance scholars. The Erasmus Finance Group and the Department of Finance at RSM are supported by the Erasmus Research Institute of Management (ERIM) through extensive research support.

### Additional information

A tenure track assistant professor position with a promotion decision in the seventh year (to tenured associate professor) based on individual performance. This is a full-time position (1.0 FTE) with a contract for 40 hours per week.

RSM’s Department of Finance has access to excellent facilities, including most major databases (WRDS, CRSP, Compustat, Eikon, I/B/E/S, Thomson One Banker, TAQ, etc.) and a modern building on Erasmus University’s campus in Rotterdam. Rotterdam is a pleasant and lively harbour city in the west of the Netherlands with 625,000 inhabitants. It provides attractive living conditions for international faculty. English is widely spoken, and air, road, and railway connections with major European and U.S. cities are excellent. The standards of healthcare and education in the Netherlands are high, while the costs are low relative to Anglo-Saxon countries.

### Applying

Are you interested in joining the Department of Finance? Be sure to formally apply for this vacancy before Sunday, 15 November 2026 by uploading your complete application package.

Please note that our colleagues at the Erasmus School of Economics are currently recruiting as well. Although we coordinate during the flyout stage, the two hiring processes are separate, and applicants are encouraged to apply to both positions if they are interested.

Your application should include:

* cover letter

* three reference letters (letters without letterhead and signature will not be considered).

Although we’re accepting applications until the positions are filled, we will start inviting candidates for online interviews within two weeks after the application deadline. Fly-outs are expected to take place as of mid-January 2027 (on campus in Rotterdam).

**Ad text:**

The Department of Economics, Faculty of Arts and Science at Queen’s University invites applications for the Stephen J.R. Smith Chair in Economic Policy. This will be a tenured appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level, with a preferred start date of July 1, 2027.

While we are seeking a scholar with demonstrated leadership in Industrial Organization, or Public Economics, or Financial and International economics, strong candidates in other related fields are also encouraged to apply.

This posting is to fill an existing vacancy within the University.

**Qualifications**

Candidates must have a PhD completed at the start date of the appointment. The main criteria for selection are academic and teaching excellence which should be demonstrated by:

* A strong record of high-quality scholarly output as shown by an independent research program and high-quality peer-assessed publications
* A strong record of success in obtaining peer-reviewed competitive grant funding from external bodies.
* An established international research program, with evidence of scholarly impact.
* Evidence of outstanding teaching contributions and a commitment to pedagogical excellence
* A strong record of graduate student supervision and training in a collaborative environment

The diverse backgrounds of applicants and the type of scholarship appropriate to their research areas, as well as the diverse range of scholarly methodologies and ways of measuring impact will be taken into account when assessing the quality of the scholarly or creative work. Candidates will be evaluated using the principles of the [**Declaration on Research Assessment**](https://sfdora.org/) **(DORA)** and with attention to the diverse ways excellence can be demonstrated. The successful candidate will also be expected to make contributions through service to the department, the Faculty, the University, and/or the broader community. The annual salary for this appointment is expected to be between $180,000-$200,000+. The actual amount will be commensurate with qualifications and experience, and may include a salary stipend, associated with the Chair.

**Vaccination Requirements**

Prior to May 1, 2022, the University required all students, faculty, staff, and visitors (including contractors) to declare their COVID-19 vaccination status and provide proof that they were fully vaccinated or had an approved accommodation to engage in in-person University activities. These requirements were suspended effective May 1, 2022, but the University may reinstate them at any point.

**Institution**

From Nobel Prize-winning research exploring the building blocks of the universe to cancer care and treatment to sustainable technologies, Queen’s University is tackling humanity’s most pressing challenges.

A member of the U15 group of Canadian research universities, Queen’s is home to a vibrant research community that includes 46 Canada Research Chairs, two Canada Excellence Research Chairs, and over 20 research institutes who work in partnership with communities, governments, and industry to advance research and innovation, making a measured impact on Canada and the world.

Queen’s is in the top 200 of the QS World University Rankings. In 2025, for the fifth straight year, Queen’s ranked among the global top 10 in the Times Higher Education (THE) Impact Rankings. THE Impact Rankings are an international ranking of universities that are advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals within and beyond their local communities. Queen's placed sixth worldwide and first in Canada out of over 2,300 universities in more than 120 countries..

At Queen’s University, we are committed to advancing Indigenization, Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Accessibility, and Anti‑Racism (I‑EDIAA) as core priorities that shape our workplace and research culture. We recognize that diversity drives innovation, strengthens collaboration, and helps remove barriers so that everyone can thrive. Our eight employee resource groups (ERGs) play a vital role in fostering belonging, amplifying diverse voices, and supporting employees across the university. Faculty and their dependents are eligible for an extensive benefits package that includes prescription drug coverage, vision care, dental care, long‑term disability insurance, life insurance, and access to the Employee and Family Assistance Program. Employees also participate in a pension plan, and tuition assistance is available for qualifying employees, their spouses, and dependent children. Queen’s values families and provides a “top up” to government parental leave benefits for eligible employees on maternity/parental leave, as well as partial reimbursement for eligible daycare expenses. Full details are outlined in the Queen’s–QUFA Collective Agreement, and more information on employee benefits can be found through Queen’s Human Resources.

**The City**

The University is situated on the traditional territories of the Haudenosaunee and Anishinaabe, in historic Kingston on the shores of Lake Ontario. Queen’s is an integral part of the Kingston community, with the campus nestled in the core of the city, only a 10-minute walk to downtown. Kingston’s residents enjoy an outstanding quality of life with a wide range of cultural and creative opportunities, with access to many natural areas and proximity to vibrant First Nations Communities including Tyendinaga and Akwesasne. Kingston is a unique Canadian city of 125,000 with a distinct blend of history, recreation, industry, and learning. Kingston offers unique waterfront living with many recreational opportunities. It is within a two-and-a-half-hour drive (two-hour train ride) to the commercial, industrial and political hubs of Toronto, Montreal, and the nation’s capital, Ottawa, and a thirty-minute drive from the international bridge linking Ontario and upstate New York. The city is also the origin of the historic Rideau Canal system – a UNESCO International Heritage site, and is close to Frontenac Provincial Park, the Thousand Islands National Park, and the Frontenac Arch UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve. The [Queen’s University Biological Station](https://tinyurl.com/2p9yb73d), north of the city, encompasses 34 km2 of diverse lands, affording premier learning and research opportunities. Visit [Inclusive Queen’s](https://www.queensu.ca/inclusive/) for information on equity, diversity and inclusion resources and initiatives.

**How to Apply**

The University invites applications from all qualified individuals. Queen’s is strongly committed to employment equity, diversity and inclusion in the workplace and encourages applications from Black, racialized/visible minority, Indigenous people, women, persons with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQ+ persons.

We recognize that certain circumstances, including career interruptions, caregiving responsibilities, health conditions, or systemic barriers, may affect a nominee’s record of research achievement. Applicants are encouraged to provide relevant information to contextualize their research record.

Queen’s is committed to providing support and accommodation for applicants with disabilities at all stages of the recruitment processes. If you require accommodation for submitting your application or during the interview process, please contact the Interim Department Manager, Carley Malone, in the Department of Economics (Dunning Hall) via econ.admin@queensu.ca.

Applications from all qualified candidates will be considered in the applicant pool. The successful candidate must be legally eligible to work in Canada at the time of appointment. In accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, priority will be given to Canadian citizens, permanent residents of Canada, and any qualified individuals who have a valid legal work status in Canada. Please indicate in your application if you have a valid legal work status in Canada.

Those interested in this position should submit a complete application package, including the following documents:

* a cover letter, including information regarding your eligibility to work in Canada and whether you would require work authorization;
* a current Curriculum Vitae including a list of publications (publications with students should be clearly indicated), awards, grants (secured and pending), and other evidence of scholarly impact; and,
* a summary of the research program, and the ways in which the program is/will be making an impact in the field; and
* a statement of teaching interests and experience (including teaching outlines and evaluations if available); and,
* a statement of experience with, and commitment to, facilitation and promotion of Indigenization, equity, diversity, inclusion, anti-racism (I-EDIAA), and accessibility and how I-EDIAA has been incorporated into the teaching and research environment; and,
* contact information for three potential people who could provide references upon request. Referees will be contacted only for shortlisted candidates, with advance notice.

We will start reviewing applications on **November 6, 2026.**

Applicants are encouraged to submit all documents in their application packages electronically as PDFs via EconJobMarket at [http://www.econjobmarket.org](http://www.econjobmarket.org/), although hard copy applications may be submitted to:

Department of Economics  
209 Dunning Hall

Kingston, Ontario  
CANADA K7L 3N6

About the University
--------------------

Founded in June 2022, HKUST (GZ) is located in Nansha, Guangzhou, the geometric center of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. It is perfectly placed for geographical convenience and forms part of an axis for technological progress. They call it the new Silicon Valley of the East.

It is the world’s first university to experiment with an innovative academic structure. With Hubs and Thrusts instead of Schools and Departments, it is geared to promoting interdisciplinary learning in a restless search for innovative solutions to humanity’s major challenges.

HKUST(GZ) boasts cutting-edge research facilities tailored to meet the needs of our investigating scientists in various disciplines. HKUST(GZ) is a spin-off from the world-class HKUST. But both benefit from the synergy of unified and complementary campuses with shared resources--another radical departure from the conventional practice in higher education. The HKUST(GZ) community will consist of 800 faculty members, 4000 undergraduates and 6000 postgraduates.

Our academic staff are drawn from the world’s finest institutions. Here English is the medium of instruction and undergraduate programs are carefully articulated with postgraduate studies.

About Society Hub
-----------------

The HKUST(GZ) Society Hub (SOCH) aims to be a global leader in addressing societal challenges in the age of intelligence. We are committed to nurture socially-conscious talents with cutting-edge analytical skills and an open and growing mindset, ready to resolve socio-economic issues and contribute to the knowledge economy in a networked society and rapidly changing world. The Hub primarily comprises four Thrusts: Carbon Neutrality and Climate Change (CNCC), Financial Technology (FTEC), Innovation, Policy and Entrepreneurship (IPE), and Urban Governance and Design (UGOD).

**About Courses**

**DLED 3030 English Communication I for Society Hub programs**

The course provides students with exposure to and practice in using English within the specific fields of Carbon Neutrality and Climate Change, Financial Technology, Innovation, Policy and Entrepreneurship, Urban Governance and Design. The course aims to encourage students to develop their abilities as thoughtful communication strategists, to communicate effectively, appropriately and confidently in relevant academic and professional contexts, and to use language to express critically the wider social implications of their fields on topics relevant to all SOCH students.

**DLED 4030 English Communication II for Society Hub Programs**

This one year course makes use of the Final Year Thesis or Final Year Capstone Project with their associated spoken and written components to maximize the language and literacy gains from carrying out this significant piece of work. The course supports students in producing the communicative components of the project and, though iterations of those components, further develops and refines their ability to present and write at a high level in an academic context.

**Job Description**

Society Hub is recruiting a Senior Lecturer/Lecturer for DLED 3030 English Communication I for Society Hub Programs and DLED 4030 English Communication II for Society Hub Programs. These are Hub-level English courses for all SOCH undergraduate students. We welcome exceptional candidates who are enthusiastic about cross-disciplinary education and innovative teaching methods, and have demonstrable expertise and teaching experiences in one of the following areas, including but not limited to:

- Carbon Neutrality and Climate Change

- Financial Technology

- Innovation, Policy and Entrepreneurship

- Urban Governance and Design

Major responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Design, teach, and assess English communication courses tailored to the academic and technical needs of Society Hub disciplines;

- Guide students in writing, presentations, and oral communication in academic and professional contexts;

- Develop and refine course materials;

- Contribute to pedagogical innovation and participate in teaching development activities;

- Support students in language-related components of international exchange programs, competitions and academic collaborations as needed;

- Conduct research on teaching innovation, educational technology, etc. to continuously improve the course delivery;

- Participate in other community services assigned by the Dean.

**Qualification of Candidates**

- A PhD degree in the fields mentioned above or any other related fields;

- Proven teaching commitment and performance in higher education sector;

- Able to inspire and cultivate the interdisciplinary mindset, critical thinking and innovation ability of students by providing them with diversified learning experiences;

- A high level of proficiency in spoken and written English;

- Be passionate in teaching and learning with outstanding communication skills and teamwork spirit.

English is the medium of instruction and administration at HKUST (GZ). HKUST(GZ) is committed to diversity in recruitment and equal opportunity employment and we strongly encourage suitable candidates of diverse backgrounds to submit their applications.

**Remuneration and Conditions of Service**

Salary is highly competitive of international standard and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Appointment to teaching-track faculty (TTF) will be made on a fixed-term contract of up to 3 years with a term review after 3 years of service, and is renewable subject to performance, mutual agreement and funding availability.

**Application Procedure**

Please submit the application via the HKUST(GZ) Recruitment System (<https://facrecruit.hkust-gz.edu.cn/>) and indicate the **Job ID (6685)**. You should first sign up to create your personal account. For more information on HKUST(GZ), you may visit the recruitment website (<https://www.hkust-gz.edu.cn/join-us/>).

Review of applications will continue until all positions are filled. We thank applicants for their interest. Please be advised that only shortlisted candidates will be notified of the result of the application.

For questions regarding the recruitment system or general inquiry, please reach us at [facultyhire@hkust-gz.edu.cn](mailto:facultyhire@hkust-gz.edu.cn). For Hub specific questions, please address to Hub’s individual email, e.g. gzrecruitsoc@hkust-gz.edu.cn with subject title of “**Application to DLED 3030 & 4030**”.
